systems.name: rubric-d-failure-paths

lens.name: silent-failures
lens.focus: Error handling and fallbacks. List every catch, .catch, default-on-error, optional chaining or ?? fallback, retry, timeout and early return that the change adds or touches. For each, ask: which unexpected errors could it hide; did the request or spec ask for this fallback; should the failure propagate or fail closed instead; is a retry limited to transient failures, bounded by one deadline, and does it keep the original failure and its classification; does every pending or in-flight state end on every path. A failed security, isolation or inspection check that ends in silent success or an unchecked path is a blocker.

lens.name: test-gaps
lens.focus: Tests. For each new or changed behaviour, find the test that would fail if that behaviour regressed, and say so when none exists. Flag tests that assert the defect they should catch, compare the code with itself, mock away the logic under test, pass for the wrong reason (invalid fixture, swallowed error, early return, wrong file), or were weakened, skipped or special-cased to pass. Name the missing or broken test case precisely. A test gap that hides a real defect in the change is at least major; report the underlying defect itself as its own finding.

lens.name: trust-boundaries
lens.focus: Secrets, untrusted input and isolation. Trace every credential, token, private value and untrusted input (issue or PR text, gate or test output, model output, configuration or scripts from the change) from its source to every sink: logs, events, errors, PR comments, commit metadata, branch names, model prompts, files and network. Check that redaction happens after decoding and before truncation, on error and retry paths as well as the normal one. Check sandbox profiles, deny lists and allowlists for path aliases, symlinks, files versus directories, environment variables and child processes. Anything that steers the factory must come from the base commit, never the change. When isolation or a check cannot be confirmed, the code must refuse with a clear reason, never fall back silently.

lens.name: requirements
lens.focus: Requirements. Restate each requirement, acceptance criterion and universal clause (every, all, never, only, ordering, on resume or restart) from the request and the specification. For each one, find the code that implements it on every entry point: resume paths, both harness backends, the daemon and scripts/, CLI and HTTP, cache-side calls. Mark it implemented, partly implemented or missing. Every missing or partly implemented clause that the request states is a finding that quotes the clause. A clause only the specification adds, which the request does not need, is at most minor.

systems.severityRubric:
# Severity by consequence and trigger (the reviewer's severity is not an input you must keep)
For each candidate ask: "would this plausibly happen in the next month of normal factory operation?" Deploys restart the daemon daily, so restart windows count unless they last milliseconds.
- critical: a realistic trigger that loses or corrupts persisted state, leaks a secret or private data, breaks a trust or confinement boundary, or stops the factory or deploys.
- high: a realistic trigger with real harm: a wrong result, a silent failure, lost or repeated work, a check the change claims to add that a realistic input bypasses, or a compatibility break with the previous release.
- medium: a real defect with a contrived trigger (an unusual input, configuration, environment or timing the request does not ask to handle), or a cost only in tests or diagnostics, such as a missing or weak test on its own, or a missing or less informative log line or error message.
- low: cosmetic, a process ask (a report, measurements, PR text), or behaviour the repository's own rules adopt.
A secret or credential stored or shown unredacted is at least high whatever the trigger. A new test that fails in normal runs stops deploys, so it is at least high.
Requirements: a requirement counts as undelivered only when the behaviour or protection it exists for is missing at head; then rate the missing behaviour by its trigger and harm like any other defect. Different wording, a different mechanism than the one the request preferred, log or message text, and places the request does not name are not undelivered requirements. Edits outside the request's scope are not an undelivered requirement either.
Failure paths are realistic triggers, not contrived ones: a failed read, command or network call, a lost response, a crash or restart, a concurrent change between two reads of shared state, and timestamps that share a second all happen in normal factory operation. A failure path the request explicitly asks the change to handle is a realistic trigger however rare it is.
A digest, report, status or feed the change produces that omits or misstates items is a wrong result, not a diagnostics cost.

Verifier: 6 candidates, 6 checked, 1 refuted.

findings.title: An excluded queued trial aborts the entire evaluation
findings.detail: `toTarget` now throws for an excluded model, but this call occurs before the trial's error handler. If a queued trial's model becomes excluded before the trial starts, the exception escapes the worker and fails the whole eval, interrupting unrelated queued or running trials instead of recording the affected trial's failure.
findings.suggestion: Handle the origin exclusion inside the trial's error boundary and record the affected trial with the exclusion reason, allowing unrelated trials to continue.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains several models or cases; while one trial is waiting behind another, its runtime model is patched from US to CN under a CN exclusion. When that trial starts, the eval fails and remaining trials are interrupted.

verification.evidence: src/router/router.ts:167-168: `const origin = originExclusion(m, this.excludeOrigins); if (origin) throw new Error(...)`. src/evals/runner.ts:617 calls `router.toTarget(model, effort ?? null)` before the trial's `try` at line 625. The worker catches the rejection at lines 499-502 with `failed = true; throw error;`; line 524 calls `store.interruptEval(run.id, (error as Error).message, "failed")`.
verification.trigger: With CN excluded, patch a queued model from US to CN before its trial reaches target construction. The exception escapes trial-level handling, stops new trials for that provider, marks the eval failed, and skips remaining queued trials.

findings.title: Verifier failure can omit the exclusion that exhausted the choices
findings.detail: The exclusion reason is propagated only when every listed verifier is excluded. If an allowed verifier remains but is ineligible because it raised the candidate, `pickVerifier` throws a different error that omits the excluded alternative. The invocation therefore fails without the required origin exclusion reason.
findings.suggestion: Include collected exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after filtering, and log excluded verifier choices.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier list contains an allowed model that raised the candidate and a CN model excluded by configuration. No verifier can be selected, but the error reports only that the allowed model raised the candidate.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1342 collects `exclusions.push(`${targetId}: ${reason}`)`, but :1347 reports them only under `if (!listed.length && exclusions.length)`. With an allowed model remaining, :1349 calls `pickVerifier(listed, avoidVendors, avoidModels, identity)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:325–327 then throws `NoCapacityError(`verifier ${targets.map((t) => t.modelId).join(", ")} raised a candidate it would check`)` without the exclusions.
verification.trigger: The verifier roster contains an excluded CN model and an allowed model that raised the candidate. The allowed model keeps listed nonempty, then independence selection fails; the error omits the CN exclusion.

findings.title: Cover a catalog origin change while a production invocation is waiting
findings.detail: The new queued-origin tests exercise eval and chat calls, but no test covers a normal pipeline invocation whose selected runtime model becomes excluded while it waits for a provider slot or before dispatch. The existing pipeline race tests change routing cells or provider preference, so they would not catch a regression in catalog-driven routing invalidation.
findings.suggestion: Add a fake-harness pipeline test that selects an allowed runtime model, blocks it before dispatch, patches its origin to an excluded value, and verifies that it is never invoked and the exclusion reason is reported.
findings.failure_scenario: A runtime model is changed from US to CN while a production run is queued. If catalog edits stop invalidating the routing revision, the stale target can be dispatched despite the configured CN exclusion without an existing test failing.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline.test.ts:9484 tests queued edits only with `test.each(["cell", "prefer"])`; lines 9497–9498 call `runtime.setCell(...)` or `runtime.setPrefer(...)`, never a catalog origin patch. Production currently relies on src/router/runtime-catalog.ts:71, `this.router.setModels(this.models)`, and src/router/router.ts:79, `this.invalidateRouting()`. src/pipeline/context.ts:742 guards dispatch with `if (revision.aborted)`, rather than rechecking the model's current origin.
verification.trigger: Coverage gap: removing catalog-change routing invalidation would allow a production invocation queued for a US model to dispatch after its catalog origin changes to excluded CN. Existing queued production tests exercise policy and preference changes, not this catalog mutation. The current implementation prevents the bypass.

findings.title: Verifier exclusions are omitted from the run log
findings.detail: The request says the skip reason in the run log reads `origin excluded (<origin>; baseOrigin=<baseOrigin>)`. This verifier-selection path removes excluded alternatives before calling the router, but logs their reasons only when every listed target is excluded. When an allowed verifier remains, the exclusion is invisible in the run log.
findings.suggestion: Record the excluded verifier alternatives and their reasons when filtering them, including when another verifier is selected.
findings.failure_scenario: A review system lists one CN verifier and one US verifier with CN excluded; the US verifier runs, but the run log does not explain that the CN verifier was skipped.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1341–1343 handles excluded verifiers with `exclusions.push(`${targetId}: ${reason}`); return [];` without logging. At :1350 only the selected verifier reaches `call(request, { ...constraints, only }, undefined)`. src/router/router.ts:386–388 routes that request through `consider([c.only]); return { candidates: ranked.map((r) => r.target), skipped };`, so the excluded roster entries never reach the `skipped: decision.skipped` log metadata in src/pipeline/context.ts:659–661.
verification.trigger: A verifier roster contains an excluded CN model and an eligible US model. The US verifier runs, but the CN verifier was filtered before routing and its exclusion is absent from the verifier invocation log.

findings.title: Verifier exhaustion can hide the origin exclusion reason
findings.detail: The request says that when exclusions leave no candidate, the invocation fails with the origin exclusion reason. This check reports exclusions only if the filtered list is empty. If the remaining allowed targets are ineligible because they raised the finding, `pickVerifier` throws a different error that omits the excluded alternatives and their reasons.
findings.suggestion: Include the collected exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after applying the independence constraints.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier list contains an excluded CN model and an allowed US model, and the US model raised the candidate being verified. Selection fails with only the raised-candidate message, despite the CN exclusion preventing the other choice.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1347 throws the collected exclusion reasons only when `!listed.length`; :1349 otherwise invokes `pickVerifier(listed, avoidVendors, avoidModels, identity)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:323–327 rejects remaining models that raised the candidate and throws only `verifier ${targets.map((t) => t.modelId).join(", ")} raised a candidate it would check`.
verification.trigger: An excluded CN verifier is removed while an allowed US verifier remains but raised the candidate. Selection fails with the raised-candidate message and loses the origin exclusion reason. This is the same defect as C2.

findings.suggestion: Check and report origin exclusions before accepting the declined-answer fallback when they are what prevents further routing.
findings.failure_scenario: An allowed review model returns a last-resort decline, and the only remaining model has an excluded origin. Routing returns the declined answer instead of failing with `origin excluded (...)`.

verification.trigger: An unpinned invocation receives a last-resort decline from an allowed model, then routing excludes every remaining candidate by origin. It returns the declined answer instead of failing with the exclusion reason. No excluded model is called.

findings.title: Filter excluded verifier alternatives before constructing eval targets
findings.detail: The request requires the router to treat an excluded model as ineligible for verifier selection. findings.suggestion: Filter excluded verifier alternatives before converting them to targets, and fail with the exclusion reason only when no eligible verifier remains.

findings.title: Reviewable text still requires a binary allowance in some mode changes
findings.detail: The new condition applies a stricter definition of text than Git's diff classification. It flags executable text containing non-UTF-8 bytes or control characters, and flags executable text under a media extension regardless of its contents. It also newly blocks a non-UTF-8 text file when an edit removes its executable bit: the old condition did not flag a mode change accompanied by a content change. These paths can be shown as text in the diff but are reported as binary content.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the mode condition to removing the inert-media exemption, and leave text classification to the existing diff classification as requested.
findings.failure_scenario: An executable shell script containing a Latin-1 character in a comment is edited and chmodded to 0644. Git treats it as text, but reviewableText returns false and the audit requires Allow: binary.

findings.title: Draft deferrals never resume when GitHub polling is disabled
findings.detail: Skipped draft triggers are no longer returned by pendingConflictTriggers, and the only code that reactivates them is in the GitHub poller. The supported github.poll = false configuration does not start that poller, so a land-triggered conflict deferred while a PR is a draft remains skipped permanently, even after the PR becomes ready or the daemon restarts.
findings.suggestion: Provide a change-observation path for installations with polling disabled, or preserve a bounded fallback for that configuration.
findings.failure_scenario: Set github.poll = false, create a land conflict trigger while the PR is a draft, then mark the PR ready on the same head. Subsequent conflict processing never sees the skipped trigger and no round starts.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/index.ts:38-45 starts `startGitHubPoller(...)` only when `factory.cfg.githubPoll` is true. src/db/store.ts:1114 selects only `WHERE state = 'pending'`; draft triggers become `state = 'skipped'` with reason `"PR is draft"` (1177-1191). src/pipeline/conflict-round.ts:14 processes only `store.pendingConflictTriggers()`. The sole caller of `recheckDraftConflictTriggers` is the poller (src/integrations/github-poller.ts:373-374).

candidates.detail: The request says to recheck a draft deferral when the poller observes “a new head.” This guard compares the snapshot only with the poller's previous snapshot. The deferred trigger remains stale until another qualifying change occurs.
candidates.suggestion: Check deferred triggers against each observed snapshot, or otherwise make recording the deferral and observing the head change race-safe.

findings.title: Treat a worker confinement failure as a terminal failure
findings.detail: A check reporting a confinement failure is rejected as an invalid result, which calls workers.fail. After the retry is exhausted, the LAN executor runs the gates locally and can return a pass. This converts a failed security check into a successful gate result.
findings.suggestion: Preserve confinement failures as a distinct terminal failure and propagate them through the gate result without retrying them into a pass.
findings.failure_scenario: Both worker attempts report a Seatbelt launch failure, but the local fallback executes successfully; the overall gate is reported as passing.

verification.evidence: src/workers/protocol.ts:65 rejects confinement failures: `.refine((r) => !r.confinementError && !launchFailure(r.output), "Worker confinement failed")`. src/server/workers.ts:131-133 handles that rejection with `workers.fail(id, ...)`. src/db/workers.ts:260 transitions using `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`. src/gates/lan.ts:73-89 then runs the local executor and returns its result: `workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);`.
verification.trigger: Both worker attempts report confinement failures. They become infrastructure failures, and a successful local fallback replaces them with a passing GateRun instead of preserving a terminal confinement failure.

findings.title: Do not discard failed checks received before an infrastructure failure
findings.detail: Check events from a worker are persisted and forwarded, but the final result is replaced by the next attempt or local fallback if that worker disconnects before posting its GateRun. A later pass therefore erases an already observed failing check, contrary to the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and account for validated failing check results across attempts when producing the final gate outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing test check and loses its connection before posting the final result; the retry or local fallback passes, so the run receives a passing GateRun.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:68–72 collects stored events separately, then returns only the final result: `events.push(...stored.slice(index))` and `if (job.state === "done" && job.result) return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun`. The local fallback likewise returns its own run at src/gates/lan.ts:86–89: `workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);`. src/gates/executor.ts:211–215 sends check events to hooks but returns `execution.result` without reconciling prior failures.
verification.trigger: A worker posts a failing check, then disconnects before submitting its GateRun. Infrastructure recovery retries elsewhere or locally; if that execution passes, the returned GateRun passes without retaining the earlier failure.

findings.title: Do not retry certificate pin failures indefinitely
findings.detail: The catch treats every workerRequest exception as a transient connection error. That includes an invalid coordinator URL or a changed pinned TLS fingerprint, so the worker silently retries forever instead of surfacing the security or configuration failure. The retry has no deadline.
findings.suggestion: Classify request errors and propagate certificate validation and configuration failures; bound retries for transient transport errors.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator presents a certificate whose fingerprint differs from the stored pin. The worker stays running and retries indefinitely without reporting the fingerprint mismatch.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:114-115 rejects a mismatched pin with `new Error("Coordinator certificate fingerprint changed")`. src/workers/client.ts:146-148 catches every request rejection and returns `undefined`; :139 loops `for (;;)`, while :157-158 sleeps and caps the retry delay at 10 seconds.
verification.trigger: A coordinator presents a certificate differing from the stored pin. The worker silently retries until externally aborted, discarding the fingerprint mismatch error.

findings.title: The credential test does not establish worker-side redaction
findings.detail: The worker and coordinator run in the same process and share the credential registry. The test registers the secret globally and checks only the stored coordinator result and events, so coordinator-side sanitization can make it pass even if the worker sends the credential in plaintext.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the outgoing worker event and result bodies before coordinator processing, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction is removed and a gate prints a worker-only credential; the shared coordinator registry still redacts the stored output, so this test passes while the credential crosses the connection.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:659 registers `registerCredential("WORKER_OUTPUT_TEST", secret)`. The helper calls `runWorker(...)` in the same process (test/workers.test.ts:459), sharing the module-level `credentialValues` registry (src/util/proc.ts:667). Assertions inspect only stored data: `expect(jobs[0]?.result).not.toContain(secret)` and the equivalent events assertion (test/workers.test.ts:681-682). Coordinator storage independently sanitizes both: `events.push(this.sanitize(event))` (src/db/workers.ts:238) and `JSON.stringify(this.sanitize(run))` (src/db/workers.ts:291).
verification.trigger: Worker-side redaction regresses and raw credential output crosses the connection; the shared coordinator registry sanitizes it before storage, so the test's assertions still pass. This establishes a test gap, not a current credential leak.

findings.title: The bundle test never exercises distinct head and base commits
findings.detail: The shared request fixture assigns the same commit to headSha and baseSha. Consequently, the end-to-end bundle test cannot detect an implementation that bundles only the head, even though the request requires both commits to be available on the worker.
findings.suggestion: Create distinct base and head commits and have a worker gate verify that both requested commits are present.
findings.failure_scenario: Bundle creation omits baseSha when it differs from headSha; the existing end-to-end test still passes because its two SHAs are identical.

verification.evidence: The bundle fixture assigns `baseSha: sha` and `headSha: sha` (test/workers.test.ts:123-124), and the end-to-end test uses `const req = await request(true)` (test/workers.test.ts:657). Production currently includes both via `const refs = [...new Set([request.headSha, request.baseSha].filter(Boolean))]` (src/server/workers.ts:88), but identical fixture SHAs exercise only one ref.
verification.trigger: Bundle creation regresses to including only headSha; the existing end-to-end test still passes because baseSha equals headSha, leaving distinct-base bundle coverage missing.

findings.title: Reconcile streamed check failures with the final result
findings.detail: The coordinator validates each check event and the final GateRun independently. It accepts a passing final result even if the same lease previously reported that check as failed. The failed event is stored, but it does not influence the returned GateRun, so an inconsistent worker response can turn an observed failure into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Validate the final run against the check events recorded for the current lease and treat inconsistent results as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid failed event for a requested check, then posts a valid GateRun reporting that same check as passed; the coordinator completes the job with the passing result.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:135-136 stores events independently from completion: `if (action === "events" && event.success) workers.event(id, event.data); else if (result.success) workers.complete(id, result.data.run);`. src/workers/validation.ts:25-48 validates the final run against requested checks without consulting stored events. src/db/workers.ts:290-291 writes that final run directly with `UPDATE gate_jobs SET state='done',result=?...`.
verification.trigger: A leased worker submits a schema-valid failed check event, then a schema-valid passing final result for the same requested check and SHA. The coordinator accepts the contradictory passing result and completes the job.

findings.title: Coordinator-only credentials can be truncated before redaction
findings.detail: runLocalGates truncates output on the worker after redacting only credentials registered on that worker. The coordinator subsequently redacts the already-truncated value using its own credentials. If the tail boundary cuts through a coordinator credential that the worker does not know, the coordinator sees only a fragment and literal credential redaction cannot remove it before the event or result is stored.
findings.suggestion: Ensure coordinator-only credentials cannot be cut before coordinator-side redaction, such as by sending bounded raw output with enough overlap for coordinator redaction before applying the final output limit.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a coordinator credential unknown to the worker, followed by enough output that the 6,000-character tail starts in the middle of that credential. The credential suffix is sent to and stored by the coordinator.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:126 stores `combined.slice(-OUTPUT_TAIL)`, with `OUTPUT_TAIL = 6_000` at :74. src/workers/client.ts:233 sends `redactGateData({ run, sha })`. A suffix alone matches neither full-secret filter.
verification.trigger: A gate prints a coordinator-only credential followed by output placing the tail boundary inside that credential. Worker redaction does not know it; coordinator redaction receives only its suffix and stores it unredacted.

findings.title: Restart discards leased retry and timeout jobs

findings.title: PR numbers cannot target unowned pull requests
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number or URL, but the unowned path accepts only a full GitHub URL. A valid number that has no matching factory run is rejected as "run not found", even when its repository is configured.
findings.suggestion: Resolve PR-number targets in the configured repository context, and report ambiguity when the repository cannot be determined.
findings.failure_scenario: Running `limitless land 7 --sha <full-head-sha>` for a hand-opened PR returns "run not found" instead of queuing it.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:183-184: `const run = this.store.getRun(input.target) ?? this.store.runForPr(this.prRef(input.target)); if (!run) return this.requestUnowned(input);` src/land/queue.ts:226-227: `const match = /^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$/.exec(input.target); if (!match) throw new Error("run not found");`
verification.trigger: Request land for bare PR number `7` with its full current SHA and no owning factory run -> the URL-only matcher rejects it with `run not found`.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories without excluding PRs from forks. This check rejects every cross-repository PR before it can enter the queue, leaving that common class of hand-opened PR without the requested confined land path.
findings.suggestion: Support the head repository when fetching and updating the approved branch, while retaining the pinned-head and publication checks.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository and has the supplied current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:251-252: `if (pr.state !== "OPEN") throw new Error(`pull request is ${pr.state}`); if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`
verification.trigger: An open fork PR targets a configured repository and supplies its exact current SHA -> it is categorically refused instead of entering the requested land pipeline.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned land entries
findings.detail: Unowned entries are stored with an empty run ID in the existing queue table. After a rollback, the previous release claims these entries and requires that ID to resolve to a run; it instead marks them blocked as "run  is gone". This loses the active land's progress, including a possible already-pushed base merge, rather than preserving it for the newer release.
findings.suggestion: Keep entries that the previous release cannot process out of its claimable queue, with a migration and resume strategy that preserves active work across rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is queued or waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release. The older queue claims the entry and permanently marks it blocked because no run has ID "".

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 persists an unowned entry as `entry.runId ?? ""`. Base src/db/store.ts:100 reads `run_id AS runId`; :2784–2785 claims queued or expired active entries, including `waiting_ci`. Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 executes `const run = this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` and `if (!run) throw new Error(`run ${entry.runId} is gone`)`. Its catch at :327 calls `this.block(...)`, and :912 persists `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)`. HEAD src/core/types.ts:464 excludes blocked entries from active states.
verification.trigger: Rollback to the base release while an unowned land is queued or waiting for CI. Once its claim is available, the older daemon claims it, cannot find run "", and durably blocks it with "run  is gone". Upgrading again does not automatically resume that entry.

findings.title: Bare PR numbers cannot request an unowned land
findings.detail: The existing CLI accepts a PR number, and the request asks for `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, but the new path accepts only a complete GitHub URL. An unowned PR has no run through which the preceding lookup can resolve its number.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, refusing clearly if the repository is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` even when PR 77 is open on the configured repository.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:184: `if (!run) return this.requestUnowned(input);` src/land/queue.ts:226-227: `const match = /^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$/.exec(input.target); if (!match) throw new Error("run not found");`
verification.trigger: Request `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` without an owning factory run -> the bare number fails the required URL match and returns `run not found`.

findings.title: Open fork PRs are categorically refused
findings.detail: The request covers open PRs on configured GitHub repositories and does not exclude PRs whose head is in a fork. This check rejects every such PR before attempting the land, leaving a common class of hand-opened PRs outside the feature.
findings.suggestion: Support the fork head repository throughout checkout and any required base-merge push, or explicitly resolve this restriction against the requested scope.
findings.failure_scenario: An open PR targeting a configured repository from a contributor's fork is rejected with `cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed`, even with its exact current SHA.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:252: `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`
verification.trigger: An open contributor fork PR targeting a configured repository is requested with its exact current SHA -> the cross-repository guard rejects it.

findings.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
findings.detail: The empty-string sentinel keeps the old schema writable, but the previous release reads it as a run ID and requires that run to exist. After a rollback, its queue claims an unowned entry and blocks it as a missing run instead of resuming it. This violates the requirement that the previous release remain working across deploy rollback.
findings.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and processing strategy for active unowned entries, or prevent the previous release from claiming entries it cannot process.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land is waiting for CI when deployment rolls back; the previous daemon claims it, looks up run `""`, and marks the entry blocked because the run is gone.

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 writes `entry.runId ?? ""`. Base src/db/store.ts:100 exposes that value through `run_id AS runId`; :2784–2785 permits claiming `waiting_ci` entries after claim expiry. Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 looks up that run and throws `run ${entry.runId} is gone` when absent. The catch at :327 calls `this.block(...)`, which persists `this.finish(id, "blocked", reason)` at :912.
verification.trigger: An unowned land awaits CI when deployment rolls back. The previous daemon claims the released or expired entry, looks up run "", and changes the entry to terminal blocked state instead of completing it.

findings.title: Blocked unowned lands disappear from the CLI digest
findings.detail: The new feed entries have a null run ID, but the digest removes every feed item without a run ID before checking whether a blocked land is actionable. Operators relying on the digest therefore do not see these failures, despite the land feed containing them.
findings.suggestion: Teach the digest to resolve unowned land entries by PR URL or land ID and display their current blocked state.
findings.failure_scenario: A confined check fails for an unowned PR; its `land.blocked` feed item exists, but `limitless digest` omits it from blocked lands.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:260 creates unowned entries with `runId: null`. src/db/store.ts:2854 preserves `runId: entry.runId` in feed items. src/cli/digest.ts:62-63 includes `label: "Blocked lands", kinds: ["land.blocked"]`, but src/cli/digest.ts:89-91 then executes `if (!item.runId) { group.items.delete(key); continue; }`.
verification.trigger: An unowned land becomes blocked after a confined check failure -> its feed item has a null runId and the digest deletes it, omitting the blocked land.

findings.title: Unowned pull requests cannot be requested by number
findings.detail: The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL, although the existing land command accepts pull request numbers and the request specifies `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`. A valid unowned PR supplied as `77` or `#77` is rejected as `run not found`. The new test at test/land-queue.test.ts:2502 asserts that rejection rather than covering acceptance.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a pull request number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, with a clear error when the repository is ambiguous, and test both supported number forms.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured repository has an open, unowned PR 77 and the user runs `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>`; the request fails before querying GitHub.

verification.evidence: src/cli/main.ts:573 passes the argument unchanged: `body: JSON.stringify({ target: sub, ...(values.sha ? { sha: values.sha } : {}) })`. src/land/queue.ts:184 routes missing runs to `requestUnowned(input)`, whose lines 226–227 require a GitHub URL and otherwise execute `if (!match) throw new Error("run not found");`.
verification.trigger: An open unowned PR 77 exists on a configured repository; `limitless land 77 --sha <current-full-sha>` fails with `run not found` before querying GitHub.

findings.title: The unowned land test does not verify actual confinement
findings.detail: The test named as a confined land uses `recordingConfinement`, whose wrapper returns the command unchanged and whose verification only records a call. It therefore passes even if the gate command can write outside its allowed roots. This leaves the request's central confined-check behavior untested for an unowned entry.
findings.suggestion: Add a real Seatbelt integration case, skipped with the existing platform reason where unavailable, that verifies both an allowed checkout write and a denied outside write during an unowned land.
findings.failure_scenario: An unowned land runs its base check without an effective sandbox, but the recording backend still records verification and the test passes.

verification.evidence: test/land-queue.test.ts:299 injects `confinement: landConfinement.backend`; line 3241 only asserts `expect(landConfinement.calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. test/confinement.ts:8–11 implements that backend as `verify: async (roots, opts) => { calls.push({ roots, opts }); }, wrap: (cmd) => cmd`, so it records verification without applying confinement.
verification.trigger: The unowned land test runs checks through a recording backend that leaves commands unchanged. Checks execute without an effective sandbox, yet the confinement assertion passes.

findings.title: Revalidate the PR base before landing
findings.detail: The unowned request snapshots the PR's base branch, but the subsequent land and merge paths do not verify that GitHub still targets that branch. GitHub can change a PR's base without changing its head SHA, so the pinned-head check does not detect a retarget. The queue can run checks from one base and then squash-merge into another, violating the requirement that the destination base's checks govern the land.
findings.suggestion: Re-read and validate the PR's base branch before the merge, and block if it differs from the branch used for the base merge and checks. Ensure the validation is tied as closely as possible to the merge operation.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator approves an unowned PR targeting main. While its land waits for CI, someone retargets it to a release branch without changing its head. The queue checks main's configuration and GitHub merges the approved head into the release branch.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:264 persists `baseBranch: pr.baseRefName`; line 430 later uses `fetchBase(this.deps.paths, repo, entry.baseBranch, signal)`. The final merge inspection at src/git/repos.ts:1463 requests only `"title,body,headRefOid,state"`; lines 1476–1478 invoke `gh pr merge` with `--match-head-commit` but no validation of the PR base.
verification.trigger: After approval and checks against main, someone retargets the PR to a release branch while CI is pending, preserving its head SHA. The merge accepts that SHA and lands into the new branch without checking that branch's base configuration.

findings.title: Accept a PR number for an unowned land
findings.detail: The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL. The CLI documents its target as a run, PR number, or URL, and the request specifies `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`. An unowned PR supplied as a number always fails with `run not found` even when it belongs to a configured repository.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR-number target against the configured repository context, and return a clear ambiguity error if it cannot be resolved uniquely.
findings.failure_scenario: A configured repository has an open hand-made PR 123. Running `limitless land 123 --sha <current-full-sha>` returns `run not found` instead of queuing it.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:183–184: `const run = this.store.getRun(input.target) ?? this.store.runForPr(this.prRef(input.target)); if (!run) return this.requestUnowned(input);`. Lines 226–227 match only a full GitHub pull-request URL and throw `"run not found"` for a bare number.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 123 --sha <current-full-sha>` targets an open hand-made PR without an owning run; the numeric target is rejected instead of queued.

findings.title: Fork pull requests are excluded from the requested feature
findings.detail: The request says an open PR on a configured GitHub repository that no factory run opened is accepted. This rejects every cross-repository PR, even when its base repository is configured and its head SHA is explicitly approved. Hand-made contributions from forks therefore cannot use the confined land queue.
findings.suggestion: Support fetching and safely pinning fork heads, or explicitly narrow the accepted PR scope.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor opens a PR from their fork against a configured repository and requests landing with its full current head SHA; the request fails with "cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed".

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:251–252: `if (pr.state !== "OPEN") throw new Error(...)`; `if (pr.isCrossRepository) throw new Error("cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed");`. The fork rejection occurs even after the target repository passes the configured-repository check at lines 228–230.
verification.trigger: An open PR from a contributor's fork targets a configured repository, and landing is requested using its full URL and current full head SHA. The request is refused solely because it originates from a fork, excluding otherwise eligible PRs from the requested feature.

findings.title: Unowned PRs cannot be requested by PR number
findings.detail: The request specifies `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, and the existing command accepts PR numbers as well as URLs. The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL, so a PR number that has no factory run is rejected as "run not found".
findings.suggestion: Resolve a PR number against the appropriate configured repository, with a clear error when the repository is ambiguous.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless land 7 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an unowned PR on the configured repository fails before looking up the PR.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:184 delegates unowned targets to `requestUnowned(input)`. Lines 226–227 apply `/^https:\/\/github\.com\/([^/]+\/[^/]+)\/pull\/[1-9]\d*$/` to `input.target` and throw `"run not found"` when it does not match.
verification.trigger: `limitless land 7 --sha <current-full-sha>` targets an unowned PR on a configured repository; the bare number fails URL validation before any GitHub lookup.

findings.title: Rollback permanently blocks an in-flight runless land
findings.detail: The request requires compatibility with the previous release. A runless entry is persisted with an empty run ID, but the previous release resumes active entries by looking up that ID and blocks the entry when no run exists. If a deployment rolls back while such a land is queued or in progress, the old daemon changes it to blocked instead of preserving it for the newer release to resume.
findings.suggestion: Make runless entries invisible to the previous release's active queue, or otherwise provide a rollback-compatible persistence and resume mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: A runless land is waiting for CI when the daemon rolls back to the base release; on startup the old queue claims it and blocks it with "run  is gone".

verification.evidence: HEAD src/db/store.ts:2721 stores runless entries using `entry.runId ?? ""`. Base src/land/queue.ts:153 resumes active entries; base src/db/store.ts:2784–2785 includes `waiting_ci` in claimable states. Base src/land/queue.ts:819–821 performs `this.store.getRun(entry.runId)` and throws when no run exists. Its error path at :327 and :912 persists the entry as `blocked`; HEAD src/core/types.ts:464 does not include blocked entries in `ACTIVE_LAND_STATES`.
verification.trigger: Rollback while a runless land is waiting for CI. After release or expiry of its claim, the old queue processes it and permanently stops automatic progress with "run  is gone", including after the newer daemon returns.

The added test at test/land-queue.test.ts:3282 explicitly asserts that rejection rather than exercising a fork PR through the land lifecycle.
candidates.suggestion: Support fork PRs while preserving the pinned-head and publication checks, and add a test covering a fork PR targeting a configured repository.
candidates.failure_scenario: A contributor opens a PR from their fork against a configured repository and supplies its full current head SHA; the request is rejected as cross-repository.

candidates.title: Runless land test does not exercise actual confinement
candidates.detail: The test named for a confined land injects `recordingConfinement`, whose `wrap` returns the command unchanged and whose `verify` only records a call. It therefore passes even if the runless gate executes without an effective sandbox, leaving the central confined-check requirement without an end-to-end regression test.
candidates.suggestion: Add a platform-appropriate real-confinement test for a runless land that proves a forbidden operation is denied and an allowed operation succeeds.
candidates.failure_scenario: The runless land gate invokes its command outside Seatbelt while still calling the fake backend's `verify`; this test reports success.

candidates.title: Revalidate the PR base before merging
candidates.detail: The queue records the base branch at request time and uses it to select the base commit and its gate configuration, but the merge path only revalidates the head SHA. GitHub permits a PR to be retargeted without changing its head. A retargeted PR can therefore merge into a branch whose base and checks were never used for the land.
candidates.suggestion: Confirm the current PR base still matches the checked branch before publication and merge, and block if it changes.
candidates.failure_scenario: An unowned PR is queued against main, then retargeted to release while its head remains unchanged. The queue checks main's configuration and head, then GitHub merges the PR into release.

candidates.title: Accept PR numbers for unowned lands
candidates.detail: The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL. The requested CLI form is `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>`, and the existing command documents and accepts a PR number. For an unowned PR, a number instead falls through to `run not found`.
candidates.suggestion: Resolve a PR number to a configured repository and canonical PR URL, refusing clearly if the repository is ambiguous.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user runs `limitless land 604 --sha <current-full-sha>` for an open PR that no factory run opened; the request fails with `run not found`.

candidates.title: Fork pull requests are categorically refused
candidates.detail: The request says the command accepts “an open PR on a configured GitHub repository that no factory run opened.” A pull request from a fork can satisfy that requirement, but this check rejects every cross-repository PR before it enters the queue.
candidates.suggestion: Support fork PR heads while retaining the approved-head lease and exact-head merge checks.
candidates.failure_scenario: A contributor opens an otherwise valid PR from a fork against a configured repository and supplies its full current head SHA; the request fails with “cross-repository pull requests cannot be landed.”

candidates.title: Rollback blocks active unowned lands
candidates.detail: The request requires compatibility with the previous release. An unowned entry is persisted with an empty run ID, but the previous release's land queue requires every entry to resolve to a run. If a deploy rolls back while such an entry is active, the old daemon resumes it, fails to find run "", and blocks it instead of continuing the land.
candidates.suggestion: Provide a rollback-compatible representation and resume strategy for active unowned entries.
candidates.failure_scenario: An unowned land is waiting for CI when the new release is rolled back; the previous daemon claims the entry and marks it blocked because its run is gone.

candidates.title: Unowned lands are absent from the UI
candidates.detail: The request says “the UI ... show[s] these entries like any other.” The change adds no UI view of land entries. The existing UI displays runs and run-specific detail, so an entry with no run cannot be reached or displayed there.
candidates.suggestion: Expose the land queue in the UI and render unowned entries with their PR, state, and absence of a run.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user queues a hand-made PR and opens the UI to check whether it landed or was blocked; the entry is not displayed.

candidates.title: Bare PR numbers do not work for unowned PRs
candidates.detail: The requested CLI form is “limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>,” and the existing command accepts PR numbers. The new path accepts only a full GitHub URL, so an unowned PR number always produces “run not found,” even when the configured repository is unambiguous.
candidates.suggestion: Resolve an unowned PR number when its repository can be determined, and give a clear ambiguity error otherwise.
candidates.failure_scenario: With one configured GitHub repository, `limitless land 123 --sha <current-full-sha>` fails for its hand-made PR 123.

findings.title: A dirty worktree can bypass detection of a cancelled worker's push
findings.detail: When reconciliation rejects an open job, the executor cancels it and calls prepare(). If the coordinator worktree is dirty, prepare() returns null before checking the remote branch, so the executor runs the local session even if the cancelled worker already pushed an unreported commit. The request requires that case to end NeedsHuman.
findings.suggestion: Check the cancelled job's remote branch for an unreported push before falling back to local execution, including when preparation cannot proceed because the worktree is dirty.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes W but has not reported it; after restart the coordinator worktree is dirty. Reconciliation cancels the leased job, prepare() returns null, and a local session starts instead of reporting the unaccepted push.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1138-1139 requires HEAD to match and `(await clean())` for resume. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:89-91 then executes `workers.cancelAgentJob(id)` and `id = undefined`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1149 returns `null` on a dirty worktree (`if (!(await clean())) return null;`) before checking the remote at :1150-1155. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:110 executes `if (!prepared) return fallback();`, whose definition at :51 calls `local()` when not aborted.
verification.trigger: A handled worker job has pushed W without an accepted report, and the coordinator worktree is dirty on restart. Reconciliation cancels the job, then prepare returns null before inspecting the remote. A local implementation session starts instead of stopping NeedsHuman for the unaccepted push.

findings.title: A fenced pending report no longer renews its lease
findings.detail: The new result request survives the fence, but the fence aborts the job controller and heldJobs() consequently omits the job from heartbeats. Those heartbeats no longer renew its lease. If result requests remain unavailable while heartbeat requests succeed, the lease expires despite the worker continuing to retry the accepted-report request, and the coordinator rejects the eventual report.
findings.suggestion: Keep a pushed job in the heartbeat's held-job list while its independently bounded result report is pending, until the result is accepted or the lease is explicitly lost.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes during an outage and its fence fires. After restart, heartbeats succeed but result requests fail transiently for longer than the remaining lease or restart grace. The coordinator expires the job; a later result receives 409 and the pushed commit cannot be adopted.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:501-504: `heldJobs()` filters on `job.reported && !job.controller.signal.aborted`; the fence aborts those controllers at :565-567. The pushed result nevertheless retries using `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` at :857-862. src/db/workers.ts:242-252 renews leases only for IDs in `c.jobs`, and :415-420 expires an unrenewed lease. src/server/workers.ts:202-203 rejects results with `409` when the lease is no longer held.
verification.trigger: A pushed job's fence fires during coordinator downtime. After restart, successful heartbeats omit that job because its controller remains aborted. If result requests keep failing beyond restart grace, its lease expires despite the live worker; the eventual report receives 409 and the pushed commit cannot be adopted.

findings.title: Late result retries can prevent worker shutdown
findings.detail: The late-result signal excludes the worker's shutdown signal as well as the job cancellation and fence signals. If the coordinator is unreachable, `call()` keeps retrying until the attempt deadline, while `runWorker` waits for every job task in its shutdown cleanup. Stopping the worker can therefore hang for the remainder of the agent attempt, potentially many minutes.
findings.suggestion: Combine the attempt-deadline signal with the worker's shutdown signal while continuing to exclude the job controller used by cancellation and the fence.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes a commit, begins retrying its result during a coordinator outage, and then receives a shutdown signal. Its result request remains active and `runWorker` does not finish until the attempt deadline expires.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:857-862 sends a pushed result with only `AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()))`. The retry loop at :507-525 checks and sleeps using that signal. Shutdown at :984-990 calls `stop.abort()`, aborts job controllers, then awaits `...allJobs().map(([, j]) => j.task)`. src/cli/main.ts:383-384 maps SIGINT/SIGTERM to the worker's outer abort controller, which the result signal excludes.
verification.trigger: A worker has pushed and is retrying its report during a coordinator outage when SIGTERM or SIGINT arrives. Shutdown aborts heartbeat and job signals but leaves the report retry active, so runWorker waits until reporting succeeds or the attempt deadline expires.

findings.title: Queued restart test completes the job before the scheduler resumes
findings.detail: The queued case leases and reports the job before calling resumed.start(), so the resumed executor sees a done job. It does not exercise reattachment to a queued job followed by pickup and completion after restart.
findings.suggestion: Start the resumed factory while the job is still queued, observe reattachment, then lease and complete that same ID and assert that no second row is created.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that replaces a stored queued job on resume could pass this integration case because the stored job has already become done.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts:940 leases the old job; :943 then awaits `report(resumed, job, request(job), await publish(bare, request(job)))`; only afterward does :945 call `resumed.start()`.
verification.trigger: In the queued restart integration case, the stored job is already done when the scheduler resumes. A regression specific to replacing queued jobs during pipeline resume could pass this case.

findings.title: Already-adopted recovery lacks negative verification cases
findings.detail: The checkpoint test exercises recovery with a valid commit and clean worktree, but does not verify that the new HEAD-already-at-result path rejects a dirty worktree or a commit that fails the shared commit-object checks. Existing adoptWorkerCommit tests exercise the ordinary adoption path.
findings.suggestion: Add recovery cases with HEAD already at the reported SHA and either a dirty worktree or an invalid commit shape, and assert that recovery refuses adoption.
findings.failure_scenario: Removing the cleanliness or commit verification from the already-moved path would still allow the new successful recovery test to pass.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts:488 asserts `headSha(state.worktreePath)` equals `first.result_sha`, then :497-498 starts recovery and expects success without introducing dirty files or invalid commit data. The separate protections are at src/pipeline/engine.ts:1201 (`await verifyWorkerCommit(...)`) and :1202 (`... || !(await clean())`). Existing negative tests in test/adopt-worker-commit.test.ts:170 exercise `adopt()`, not this engine recovery branch.
verification.trigger: Removing verification or cleanliness checks specifically from the already-moved recovery branch would leave the successful recovery test passing. Negative tests do not exercise those protections on that branch.

findings.title: Late-report coverage does not test the attempt deadline
findings.detail: The pushed and fenced cases verify that a report survives a restart and fence, but neither holds the coordinator offline until the attempt deadline. The new independent report signal must also stop retrying at that deadline.
findings.suggestion: Add a controlled deadline case that keeps result delivery unavailable through expiry and checks that retries terminate without an accepted result.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression using an unbounded signal for pushed results would still pass the current restart cases and could leave a worker retrying indefinitely.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts:774 covers `['running', 'pushed', 'fenced']`; :850-853 waits for publication and optionally fires the fence, then :870 restores connectivity with `offline = false`. It never expires the attempt deadline. The untested bound is src/workers/client.ts:861: `AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()))`.
verification.trigger: Replacing the pushed-result timeout signal with an unbounded signal would still pass these restart cases because connectivity returns before the deadline. They do not verify that reporting stops when the attempt deadline expires.

findings.title: Restart grace expires after heartbeat freshness, before one lease period
findings.detail: The request says “a worker that stays unreachable for one lease period after the restart is retried on another worker.” Although the lease-expiry calculation grants 60 seconds, this freshness check fails the job after 30 seconds without a heartbeat. That can discard a worker’s pushed result before the promised lease period has elapsed. The requested freshness formula also specifies this 30-second behavior, so the requirements conflict and need to be reconciled.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the conflicting requirements and make the retry timing and documentation agree; add a test covering an unreachable worker between the freshness and lease deadlines.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes while the coordinator is down and remains unreachable for 31 seconds after restart. The next sweep fails its job as disconnected, even though the 60-second restart lease grace has not elapsed; a subsequent result is rejected.

verification.evidence: src/workers/protocol.ts:104-105 sets `fresh: 30_000` and `lease: 60_000`. src/db/workers.ts:415-425 extends lease expiry using `resumedAt + this.times.lease`, but independently fails freshness when `now - Math.max(w.last_heartbeat_at ?? 0, this.resumedAt ?? Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY) > this.times.fresh`, calling `failAgentJob(j.id, "Worker disconnected")`. That transition clears the worker and lease (src/db/workers.ts:385-389). Result acceptance calls `holdsAgentJob`, which sweeps first (src/db/workers.ts:346-349), and rejects a lost lease with HTTP 409 (src/server/workers.ts:200-206).
verification.trigger: An approved worker has a leased job, a pre-restart heartbeat, and an unexpired attempt deadline. It remains unreachable until 31 seconds after restart. A sweep then revokes its attempt despite the 60-second lease grace; its subsequent pushed-result report is rejected, losing the accepted report needed for adoption.

Verifier: 21 candidates, 21 checked, 5 refuted.

findings.title: Lifecycle transitions can disappear between polls
findings.detail: Comments are derived from the current run status, and an event is persisted only when reconciliation observes that status. A run that enters needs_human and is resumed or resolved before the next poll never records or posts that event. Likewise, a second needs_human episode is suppressed by the first episode's done checkpoint. This does not provide a durable side effect for each transition across restarts or polling intervals.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle events durably when transitions occur, with an identity for each status episode, and reconcile those records independently of the current status.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters needs_human and the owner resumes it before the next queue poll; no needs-you comment is posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:101–102: `if (run.status === "needs_human") events.set("needs_human", ...)`; line 113: `if (!events.has(event) && state(effect) !== "pending") continue;`. Events are derived from the current status; an unobserved transition has no pending checkpoint.
verification.trigger: A run enters needs_human and resumes between polls. Reconciliation sees the resumed status and never posts the needs-you reason or applies its label.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates only run for queue-enabled repositories
findings.detail: Both the reconciler and its timer are conditional on the issue queue's repository and trusted-account configuration. Runs started through CLI, MCP, or GitHub triggers in any other configured repository therefore receive no lifecycle labels or comments, even though the requested behavior covers every start path and does not require queue admission to be enabled.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and select linked issues according to the supported repository settings.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository has the GitHub integration configured but is absent from githubQueue.repos; a CLI run with `Closes #42` produces no lifecycle updates.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:10–12: `!!cfg.githubQueue?.trusted.length && cfg.githubQueue.repos.some(...)`; line 43: `if (!lifecycleManaged(cfg, repo)) continue;`. src/integrations/index.ts:66–67 mounts the queue only when `!!queue?.repos.length && !!queue.trusted.length`.
verification.trigger: A CLI run contains Closes #42 in a GitHub-integrated repository absent from githubQueue.repos. Its lifecycle labels and comments are skipped.

findings.title: A partial failure can release an issue before its failure label is applied
findings.detail: The label loop removes in-progress before adding failed. If the add fails, reconciliation logs the failure and queue selection continues in the same poll. The existing latest-run admission check only finds issue-source runs, so it does not protect a failed CLI or MCP run linked through its prompt. The issue can be selected again using its old priority approval before the failed label is retried.
findings.suggestion: Keep admission closed until the failure transition is durably reflected, including for prompt-linked runs; order label writes so a partial transition does not release the issue.
findings.failure_scenario: A CLI run with `Closes #42` fails; deleting in-progress succeeds but adding failed returns an error. The same poll sees the old priority label and starts a queue run without re-approval.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:13 orders labels as in-progress, needs-you, failed; lines 80–86 delete unwanted labels before adding failed and propagate an add failure to the logging catch at lines 93–94. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:191 reconciles before selecting issues; lines 96–99 enforce failure re-approval only when failed is present. src/db/store.ts:1268: `WHERE json_extract(runs.source_ref, '$.kind') = 'issue'` restricts latestIssueRun to issue-sourced runs.
verification.trigger: A CLI Closes #42 run fails, in-progress deletion succeeds, and failed addition fails. With an existing trusted priority label and no previous issue-sourced run or other blocker, that poll admits a queue run without re-approval.

findings.title: An older run can overwrite a newer run's issue labels
findings.detail: The latest-run map is computed once before any GitHub requests. If another run for the issue is created while a label request is awaiting, the old run remains designated latest and can complete its label transition after the newer run starts. Its completed cursor then prevents correction until the newer run is reconciled on a later poll.
findings.suggestion: Recheck which run owns the issue after awaited operations and before each label mutation and completion checkpoint.
findings.failure_scenario: While reconciliation fetches labels for a failed run, a new run for the same issue starts; the old reconciliation then applies failed and removes in-progress for the active run.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:35–39 builds `latest` once from `store.issueLifecycleRuns()`. Line 56 checks that snapshot before awaiting the label fetch at line 60. Lines 63–71 subsequently re-read only `store.getRun(snapshot.id)` and compare its desired label; they never recheck whether a newer run now owns the issue.
verification.trigger: A newer linked run starts while reconciliation awaits labels for an older failed run. The stale ownership check lets the old run remove in-progress and apply failed for the active run, until a later poll repairs the labels.

findings.title: Persist lifecycle events when they occur, not only when a poll observes them
findings.detail: The needs-human, failure, and cancellation comments are created only when reconciliation observes the corresponding current status. No pending effect exists until the comment loop reaches that event. A status that changes between polls, or while an earlier comment write is failing, is therefore never recorded or retried. The single done cursor also suppresses a second needs-human episode for the same run.
findings.suggestion: Record each lifecycle event and its publication-safe content durably at the state transition, then let polling deliver each recorded event.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human and is resumed before the next poll; reconciliation sees the resumed status and never posts the required reason. Similarly, a failed started-comment write can delay processing until after needs_human has ended.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:101–102 creates needs_human events only from the observed status. Line 110 processes started before needs_human; lines 165–167: `catch (error) { failure(error); break; }`. The pending checkpoint is written only when that individual event reaches lines 159–162.
verification.trigger: A needs_human interval ends before a poll observes it, or a failed started-comment write prevents the needs_human event from being checkpointed before the owner resumes. Later reconciliation omits the required needs-you comment and reason.

findings.title: Reconcile issue-linked runs outside queue-enabled repositories
findings.detail: Lifecycle processing is restricted to repositories listed in githubQueue with a nonempty trusted list, and the reconciler is started only when that queue is enabled. The request applies lifecycle updates to issue-linked runs from every start path; it does not condition those updates on queue admission being enabled for the repository.

findings.title: Status transitions between polls are lost
findings.detail: Comments and labels are derived only from the run's current status. No durable event is recorded when a run enters needs_human or failed, so a transition that ends before the next poll cannot be reconstructed. The single comment key for each status also suppresses later occurrences of the same status.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle transitions durably when they occur and reconcile each recorded occurrence independently.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters needs_human and is resumed before the next queue poll. The poll sees running and never posts the needs-you comment or applies its label. A second needs_human episode after an observed first episode also receives no new comment.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:101–102 only creates the event when `run.status === "needs_human"`. Lines 112–114 use `const effect = `comment:${event}`` and `if (state(effect) === "done") continue;`, deduplicating all needs_human episodes together. Lines 18–19 also derive the label solely from current status.
verification.trigger: A run enters and leaves needs_human between polls, so neither its label nor comment is emitted. If an earlier needs_human comment completed, a later episode's comment is permanently skipped.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-configured repositories
findings.detail: The reconciler skips every repository that is absent from githubQueue.repos or has no trusted queue accounts, and it is not started at all when the queue is disabled. The requested lifecycle applies to runs started through every entry point; it is not limited to repositories enabled for automatic issue picking.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration for linked issues.
findings.failure_scenario: A user starts `limitless run` with `Closes #7` in a repository that has no issue queue configured. The run receives no lifecycle labels or comments.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:10–12 defines lifecycleManaged using `!!cfg.githubQueue?.trusted.length && cfg.githubQueue.repos.some(...)`; line 43 skips unmatched repositories with `if (!lifecycleManaged(cfg, repo)) continue;`. src/integrations/index.ts:66–67 starts the lifecycle-owning queue only when queue repositories and trusted accounts are configured.

findings.title: A failed label write can allow a failed manual run to be re-picked
findings.detail: The transition removes in-progress before adding failed, and a write failure is caught before the queue continues to query candidates. The queue's latestIssueRun lookup only recognizes issue source references, so a terminal CLI or MCP run linked through `Closes #n` supplies no local re-approval guard.
findings.suggestion: Make admission account for terminal runs linked through all supported start paths, including while lifecycle writes are pending.
findings.failure_scenario: A CLI run for `Closes #7` fails. Removing in-progress succeeds, adding failed fails, and the issue still has its old trusted priority label. The same poll can pick it again without a new approval.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:13 orders labels as `["limitless:in-progress", "limitless:needs-you", "limitless:failed"]`; lines 68–86 remove earlier labels before attempting the failed-label POST, and lines 93–94 only log failure. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:191 reconciles before selecting candidates; lines 96–99 require re-approval only when the failed label exists. src/db/store.ts:1268 restricts latestIssueRun to `json_extract(runs.source_ref, '$.kind') = 'issue'`, excluding ordinary CLI Closes directives.
verification.trigger: A failed CLI-linked run has no issue sourceRef. Removing in-progress succeeds but adding failed fails. With no active claim, no latest issue-sourced run, and its original trusted priority label intact, the issue can be selected again in the same poll without re-approval.

findings.title: An older run can overwrite labels after a newer run starts
findings.detail: The latest-run map is computed once before any GitHub awaits. Re-reading the old run's status does not check whether another run has since claimed the same issue, so an in-flight reconciliation can apply an old terminal label after a newer run has started.
findings.suggestion: Recheck issue ownership after awaited operations and before each label mutation, coordinating it with run admission.
findings.failure_scenario: While reconciliation of an old failed run is awaiting its label read, a new run for the same issue starts. The old reconciliation then removes in-progress or adds failed based on its stale latest-run map.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:35–39 builds `latest` once from `store.issueLifecycleRuns()`. Line 56 checks that snapshot before the awaited label read at line 60. Lines 63–71 then reread only `store.getRun(snapshot.id)` and check its desired label, without checking whether a newer issue-linked run now exists.
verification.trigger: A newer run for the issue is created while an old failed run awaits its label read. Reconciliation can still remove in-progress and add failed for the old run, leaving incorrect labels until a later poll handles the newer run.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-enabled repositories
findings.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation skips every repository absent from githubQueue.repos, and the reconciler itself is started only when the queue has configured repositories and trusted accounts. The request requires lifecycle updates for every start path, including CLI and MCP runs, with gh as the fallback identity.

findings.failure_scenario: A user runs `limitless run` with `Closes #7` for a repository that is not in githubQueue.repos. No lifecycle label or comment is posted.

findings.title: Transient lifecycle events disappear before they are checkpointed
findings.detail: Events are inferred only from the current run snapshot. A needs_human or failed state that begins and ends between polls is never recorded. The same loss occurs when an earlier comment fails: the loop breaks before saving later events as pending, so a status change before the next poll erases them.
findings.suggestion: Durably record each lifecycle transition when it occurs, then reconcile its effects independently of the current status.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human while the started comment write is failing, then is resumed before the next poll. No needs-you comment is ever posted.

findings.title: A second needs-human episode is treated as already delivered
findings.detail: Comment checkpoints are keyed only by run and event name. Once a needs_human comment is marked done, a resumed run that later reaches needs_human again cannot post its new reason. Label reconciliation can still switch back to needs-you, leaving the issue with a stale explanation.
findings.suggestion: Key lifecycle effects by a durable transition or status episode rather than only by event type.
findings.failure_scenario: A run needs human input, resumes after the owner responds, and later needs human input for a different reason. The second reason is never commented.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:112 uses `const effect = `comment:${event}`;` and line 114 skips `if (state(effect) === "done") continue;`. src/db/migrations/20261024T224811-issue-lifecycle.sql:7 keys effects by `(run_id, repo, number, effect)`, with no episode identifier.

findings.title: Re-approval can come from a priority label that is no longer applied
findings.detail: The post-failure check accepts any trusted priority labeled event, even if that label was subsequently removed. The separate approved check can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before the failure, so the current approval need not be the one applied after failure.
findings.suggestion: Require a currently applied, trusted priority label whose latest application occurred after the failure label.
findings.failure_scenario: Priority:2 was applied before failure; a trusted user applies and removes priority:1 after failure. The issue remains eligible using the old priority:2 label despite the later approval having been withdrawn.

Separately, :99 accepts `events.some((e) => trusts(e.actor?.login) && Date.parse(e.createdAt) > failedAt)` without checking that event's label remains applied. :129 requests only `LABELED_EVENT, RENAMED_TITLE_EVENT`, so removals cannot invalidate that historical approval.
