findings.title: An unrelated comment can impersonate a completed lifecycle write
findings.detail: Recovery treats any issue comment containing the predictable marker as proof that the factory posted its pending comment, without checking its author. An issue participant can supply that marker and cause the actual lifecycle comment to be permanently marked done.
findings.suggestion: Verify the recovered comment was authored by the configured factory identity and matches the pending body before marking the effect done.
findings.failure_scenario: After a comment POST fails, another issue participant posts a comment containing the run's marker. On the next poll the factory records the failed comment as delivered and never retries it.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:123 parses comments as `z.object({ body: z.string() })`; lines 128–130 accept `comments.some((c) => c.body.includes(marker))`, then `save(effect, "done")`. No author or complete-body verification occurs.
verification.trigger: After a failed POST leaves a pending checkpoint, another participant posts the predictable lifecycle marker. Reconciliation treats that unrelated comment as successful delivery and permanently skips the intended comment.

findings.title: A 404 during label removal is silently recorded as success
findings.detail: The catch treats every HTTP 404 as an already-removed label. GitHub can also return 404 for an inaccessible repository or issue, so a permission or installation failure can be checkpointed as a successful label transition and will not be retried.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the label is absent with a successful fresh read before recording the removal as complete; otherwise log and retry the error.
findings.failure_scenario: The initial label read succeeds, but the App loses repository access before the DELETE. GitHub returns 404 and the reconciliation cursor records the label set as complete even though the label remains.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:86 suppresses removal errors matching HTTP 404: `if (add || !/\bHTTP 404\b/.test(String(error))) throw error;`. Line 88 saves the effect as done, and line 92 saves the complete label cursor. Line 56 skips reconciliation when that cursor matches the desired label.
verification.trigger: For cancellation or merge, the label read succeeds but repository access is lost before DELETE. The resulting 404 is treated as successful removal; the remaining in-progress label is never retried while the desired state stays unchanged.

findings.title: Status transitions between polls never produce their comments
findings.detail: Lifecycle comments are derived from the current run status. A needs_human episode that begins and ends between polls is never recorded as pending, so its required comment is permanently lost. The pending-comment tests cover a transition only after a poll has already observed it.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle events durably when transitions occur and reconcile those records. Add a test that enters and leaves needs_human between polls, then restarts and checks for exactly one comment.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human and is resumed before the next issue-queue poll; no needs-you comment is posted.

findings.title: A removed priority label can supply re-approval
findings.detail: The re-approval check accepts any trusted priority-label event after failure, even if that label is no longer present. The separate approved-label check can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before failure. The tests only exercise re-approval using the currently present label and miss this combination.

verification.trigger: Trusted priority:1 remains from before failure. A trusted user applies and removes priority:2 after failure and the latest run's completion. The removed priority:2 supplies re-approval, so the failed issue becomes eligible using old priority:1.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside the issue queue configuration
findings.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation requires the repository to be in githubQueue.repos with trusted accounts configured, and the poller does not start without that configuration. The request requires updates for linked runs from all start paths. The new test explicitly asserts no updates for disabled or unlisted repositories, thereby protecting this omission.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation for linked GitHub issues independently of queue admission configuration, and test a CLI or MCP run when queue polling is disabled.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner starts a run with Closes #7 in a GitHub repository that is not enabled for automatic issue picking; the issue receives neither labels nor comments.

findings.title: Restart coverage does not exercise each lifecycle transition
findings.detail: The interruption matrix only interrupts the initial started event. The needs-human, failure, cancellation, PR, and merge tests restart after their writes have completed, so they do not establish that a restart between each transition's label change and comment preserves the required effect.
findings.suggestion: Exercise interruption after the label update and before the comment for each applicable transition, then reopen the store and verify the final labels and exactly one comment.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that loses a failed or needs-human comment after its label write can pass the current restart tests.

verification.evidence: test/issue-queue.test.ts:1275 parameterizes interruption only by ["after label", "after comment"], and line 1298 checks only "comment:started". Terminal-transition tests restart after asserting both comments already exist (lines 1225–1229). The additional failed/needs_human restart tests require `comment:${status}` to be "pending" before restarting (lines 1347–1350), so they do not cover interruption between label completion and comment checkpoint creation.
verification.trigger: A regression affecting failed/needs_human recovery after the label write but before the comment's pending checkpoint could pass these tests; that interruption window is exercised only for run start.

findings.title: Do not accept an arbitrary issue comment as proof of a factory write
findings.detail: Recovery treats any comment containing the predictable lifecycle marker as proof that the factory posted its comment. Issue comments are untrusted: their author is neither retrieved nor checked. An attacker who can comment can therefore suppress a pending lifecycle notification.
findings.suggestion: Authenticate the author of a matching comment against the GitHub identity used for the write, and require an exact, validated marker before recording the effect as done.
findings.failure_scenario: A comment POST fails or the daemon restarts after marking it pending. Another issue participant posts a comment containing `<!-- limitless-lifecycle:<run-id>:failed -->`. On the next poll, reconciliation marks the failed notification done without posting it.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:120 constructs `<!-- limitless-lifecycle:${run.id}:${event} -->`. Lines 122–128 parse comments using only `z.object({ body: z.string() })` and check `comments.some((c) => c.body.includes(marker))`; lines 129–130 then execute `save(effect, "done"); continue;` without checking authorship.
verification.trigger: A failed POST or restart leaves a comment pending. Another participant posts its predictable lifecycle marker. The next poll treats that arbitrary comment as the factory's completed write and permanently suppresses the intended notification.

findings.title: Tie re-approval to a priority label that is still applied
findings.detail: The post-failure check accepts any historical trusted priority-label event, even if that label has since been removed. The separately computed `approved` set can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before the failure, so a withdrawn re-approval still permits the issue to run.
findings.suggestion: Require the latest trusted application of a currently applied priority label to be later than the failure event.
findings.failure_scenario: An issue retains `priority:2` from before failure. A trusted account applies `priority:1` after failure and subsequently removes it to withdraw approval. The old `priority:2` satisfies `approved`, while the historical `priority:1` event satisfies this check, so the failed issue is picked again.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:99 requires only `trusts(e.actor?.login) && Date.parse(e.createdAt) > failedAt`; it does not tie the event to the current labels checked at :74–81. :122 returns eligibility using `Math.min(...approved.map((l) => Number(l.name.slice(9))))`.
verification.trigger: Trusted priority:2 remains from before failure. A trusted account applies priority:1 after failure and completion, then removes it. Historical priority:1 satisfies re-approval and current priority:2 satisfies approval, allowing another run despite the withdrawal.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are limited to repositories in the issue queue
findings.detail: The request covers “any start path,” but reconciliation skips every repository outside `githubQueue.repos`, and the reconciler is not started at all when the queue is disabled. A CLI, MCP, label-triggered, or comment-triggered run against another repository therefore receives none of the required lifecycle labels or comments.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and cover linked issues from every supported start path.
findings.failure_scenario: A user starts `limitless run` with `Closes #12` for a repository that is not configured in `githubQueue.repos`; no in-progress label or lifecycle comments are posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:12 requires `cfg.githubQueue.repos.some((r) => r.toLowerCase() === repo.toLowerCase())`; line 43 applies `if (!lifecycleManaged(cfg, repo)) continue;`. Although src/db/store.ts:358–360 links non-GitHub runs through `closedIssues(run.prompt)`, those links still encounter this repository filter.
verification.trigger: A CLI run contains Closes #12 for a repository absent from githubQueue.repos. The linked issue is discovered but skipped, so no in-progress label or lifecycle comments are written.

findings.title: Transitions occurring between polls are never recorded
findings.detail: The requirement says each lifecycle event is a durable side effect and must not lose a label change or comment across restarts. The reconciler derives needs-human, failed, and cancelled events solely from the current run status; it creates no pending effect when the transition occurs. If the run advances again before the next poll, that event is permanently invisible.
findings.suggestion: Durably enqueue lifecycle effects at the state transition and reconcile those recorded effects on each poll.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches `needs_human` and is resumed before the next queue poll, or the daemon restarts and the run is resumed before reconciliation. No needs-you label or reason comment is ever posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:191 invokes reconciliation during the poll; line 295 schedules the next poll using `now() + q.pollSeconds * 1000`. src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:97–102 reads the current run and adds needs_human only with `if (run.status === "needs_human") events.set(...)`. Line 113 skips an absent event unless already pending: `if (!events.has(event) && state(effect) !== "pending") continue;`. Lines 15–19 likewise derive the needs-you label solely from current status.

candidates.title: Status transitions between polls are lost
candidates.detail: Comments and labels are derived only from the run's current status. No durable event is recorded when a run enters needs_human or failed, so a transition that ends before the next poll cannot be reconstructed. The single comment key for each status also suppresses later occurrences of the same status.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-configured repositories
candidates.detail: The reconciler skips every repository that is absent from githubQueue.repos or has no trusted queue accounts, and it is not started at all when the queue is disabled. The requested lifecycle applies to runs started through every entry point; it is not limited to repositories enabled for automatic issue picking.

candidates.title: A failed label write can allow a failed manual run to be re-picked

The queue's latestIssueRun lookup only recognizes issue source references, so a terminal CLI or MCP run linked through `Closes #n` supplies no local re-approval guard.

candidates.title: An older run can overwrite labels after a newer run starts
candidates.detail: The latest-run map is computed once before any GitHub awaits. Re-reading the old run's status does not check whether another run has since claimed the same issue, so an in-flight reconciliation can apply an old terminal label after a newer run has started.
candidates.suggestion: Recheck issue ownership after awaited operations and before each label mutation, coordinating it with run admission.
candidates.failure_scenario: While reconciliation of an old failed run is awaiting its label read, a new run for the same issue starts. The old reconciliation then removes in-progress or adds failed based on its stale latest-run map.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-enabled repositories
candidates.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation skips every repository absent from githubQueue.repos, and the reconciler itself is started only when the queue has configured repositories and trusted accounts. candidates.title: Transient lifecycle events disappear before they are checkpointed
candidates.detail: Events are inferred only from the current run snapshot. A needs_human or failed state that begins and ends between polls is never recorded. The same loss occurs when an earlier comment fails: the loop breaks before saving later events as pending, so a status change before the next poll erases them.

candidates.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human while the started comment write is failing, then is resumed before the next poll. No needs-you comment is ever posted.

candidates.title: A second needs-human episode is treated as already delivered
candidates.detail: Comment checkpoints are keyed only by run and event name. Once a needs_human comment is marked done, a resumed run that later reaches needs_human again cannot post its new reason. Label reconciliation can still switch back to needs-you, leaving the issue with a stale explanation.

findings.detail: Every `moved` result from a replay marks the confirmed lease lost and clears the intent without examining the returned tip. The claim client can return `moved` for a malformed record or a valid record that does not meet the supersession conditions. Clearing the journal also makes the row forgettable, losing confirmed ownership history and the final release record.

findings.title: A superseded unsent question set can never be published later
findings.detail: An unsent question effect is permanently marked done when its run temporarily stops waiting. If the run later returns to waiting with the same unanswered question IDs, observe() sees the existing effect and never creates another publication. The same problem occurs after recovery establishes that a stale POST was not accepted. The run can therefore remain waiting indefinitely without its questions appearing on the issue.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a superseded effect with no confirmed publication from a completed publication, and allow a fresh eligible waiting episode to publish the set after any uncertain prior POST has been recovered.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters waiting_input with question 42, but its pending comment has not been posted. The run temporarily changes to running, so reconciliation marks the effect done. It returns to waiting_input with question 42 still unanswered; subsequent polls and restarts never post the question.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:355–358: `let stale = pending.state === "recovering" || !eligible(); if (stale && !pending.page) { save(effect, "done"); continue; }`. At :129, publication requires `!effects.has(`comment:questions:${ids}`)`, so the completed checkpoint prevents recreation.
verification.trigger: An unsent question set becomes ineligible while the run is running, then becomes eligible again with the same IDs. Its done checkpoint permanently prevents publication.

findings.title: Retired unsent question sets cannot be published if they become eligible again
findings.detail: Superseding an unsent question effect marks it done, and observe() will never create that effect again because it already exists. A temporary linkage or status change can therefore permanently suppress a question set that was never posted.

findings.title: An excluded queued trial aborts the entire evaluation
findings.detail: `toTarget` now throws for an excluded model, but this call occurs before the trial's error handler. If a queued trial's model becomes excluded before the trial starts, the exception escapes the worker and fails the whole eval, interrupting unrelated queued or running trials instead of recording the affected trial's failure.
findings.suggestion: Handle the origin exclusion inside the trial's error boundary and record the affected trial with the exclusion reason, allowing unrelated trials to continue.
findings.failure_scenario: An eval contains several models or cases; while one trial is waiting behind another, its runtime model is patched from US to CN under a CN exclusion. When that trial starts, the eval fails and remaining trials are interrupted.

verification.evidence: src/router/router.ts:167–168: `const origin = originExclusion(m, this.excludeOrigins); if (origin) throw new Error(...)`. src/evals/runner.ts:617 calls `router.toTarget(model, effort ?? null)` before the trial's `try` at line 625. The escaped error stops provider scheduling at lines 499–502; lines 518–524 call `store.interruptEval(run.id, (error as Error).message, "failed")`.
verification.trigger: With CN excluded, patch a queued runtime model from US to CN before its trial reaches toTarget. The exception escapes trial handling, fails the evaluation, and interrupts remaining queued work instead of recording only that trial's failure.

findings.title: Verifier failure can omit the exclusion that exhausted the choices
findings.detail: The exclusion reason is propagated only when every listed verifier is excluded. If an allowed verifier remains but is ineligible because it raised the candidate, `pickVerifier` throws a different error that omits the excluded alternative. The invocation therefore fails without the required origin exclusion reason.
findings.suggestion: Include collected exclusion reasons when verifier selection fails after filtering, and log excluded verifier choices.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier list contains an allowed model that raised the candidate and a CN model excluded by configuration. No verifier can be selected, but the error reports only that the allowed model raised the candidate.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1342-1349 collects exclusions in `exclusions.push(`${targetId}: ${reason}`)` but reports them only when `!listed.length && exclusions.length`; otherwise it calls `pickVerifier(listed, avoidVendors, avoidModels, identity)`. src/pipeline/review.ts:325-328 throws only `verifier ${targets.map((t) => t.modelId).join(", ")} raised a candidate it would check` when no remaining target is independent.

findings.title: A saved head change can be lost before the draft deferral is rechecked
findings.detail: The poller saves the new snapshot before reactivating draft triggers, and uses the saved snapshot on the next pass to decide whether the head changed. If the process stops between those operations, the next pass sees the same head and an open draft, so it never rechecks the deferred trigger. The same ordering can occur when a live lookup finishes after the poller has saved the newer head and marks the trigger as draft. The trigger remains skipped despite the poller having observed a new head.
findings.suggestion: Make recording the observation and reactivating eligible draft triggers durable together, or compare each deferred trigger's recorded head with the current observation on every poll.
findings.failure_scenario: A trigger is skipped as draft at head A. The poller observes draft head B and saves it, then the daemon restarts before rechecking triggers. Subsequent observations of draft head B do not reactivate the trigger.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/github-poller.ts:345: `const same = prev?.headRefOid === head;`; :372–374: `save(unknown ? (prev?.nudged ?? null) : null); if (!same || snap.isDraft === false || snap.state !== "OPEN") store.recheckDraftConflictTriggers(pr.url, snap);`. src/db/store.ts:2675 commits the save transaction before reactivation. src/db/store.ts:1114 selects only `WHERE state = 'pending'`, excluding the stranded draft deferral.
verification.trigger: A hard interruption after saving draft head B but before reactivating the trigger leaves the saved head at B and the trigger skipped at A. After restart, unchanged draft-B observations have `same === true`, so reactivation is skipped. Becoming ready or closing still reactivates it. The interruption window is between synchronous calls, making this a narrow crash case.

findings.title: Treat a worker confinement failure as a terminal failure
findings.detail: A check reporting a confinement failure is rejected as an invalid result, which calls workers.fail. After the retry is exhausted, the LAN executor runs the gates locally and can return a pass. This converts a failed security check into a successful gate result.
findings.suggestion: Preserve confinement failures as a distinct terminal failure and propagate them through the gate result without retrying them into a pass.
findings.failure_scenario: Both worker attempts report a Seatbelt launch failure, but the local fallback executes successfully; the overall gate is reported as passing.

verification.evidence: src/workers/protocol.ts:65 rejects confinement results with `.refine((r) => !r.confinementError && !launchFailure(r.output), "Worker confinement failed")`. src/server/workers.ts:131-133 handles this as ordinary invalid data: `workers.fail(id, ...)`. src/db/workers.ts:260 transitions attempts using `j.attempt < 2 ? "queued" : "failed"`. src/gates/lan.ts:86-89 then accepts the local outcome unchanged: `workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);`.
verification.trigger: Both worker attempts report confinement launch failures; these become retryable infrastructure failures. If local fallback passes, its passing GateRun becomes the final result without preserving a terminal confinement failure.

findings.title: Do not discard failed checks received before an infrastructure failure
findings.detail: Check events from a worker are persisted and forwarded, but the final result is replaced by the next attempt or local fallback if that worker disconnects before posting its GateRun. A later pass therefore erases an already observed failing check, contrary to the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Preserve and account for validated failing check results across attempts when producing the final gate outcome.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing test check and loses its connection before posting the final result; the retry or local fallback passes, so the run receives a passing GateRun.

verification.evidence: src/gates/lan.ts:68–72 reads prior events into the event stream, then returns only the final result: `events.push(...stored.slice(index));` and `if (job.state === "done" && job.result) return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun;`. The local fallback likewise returns only its new run at src/gates/lan.ts:86–89: `workers.complete(handle.id, run, true); return workers.sanitize(run);`. src/gates/executor.ts:211–215 forwards check events to hooks but returns `execution.result` without reconciling earlier failures.
verification.trigger: A worker posts a failed check, then disconnects before submitting its GateRun. Its job is retried; a replacement worker or local fallback passes. The returned GateRun contains the passing result without preserving the observed failure, violating the requirement that infrastructure retries never turn a failing check into a pass.

findings.title: Do not retry certificate pin failures indefinitely
findings.detail: The catch treats every workerRequest exception as a transient connection error. That includes an invalid coordinator URL or a changed pinned TLS fingerprint, so the worker silently retries forever instead of surfacing the security or configuration failure. The retry has no deadline.
findings.suggestion: Classify request errors and propagate certificate validation and configuration failures; bound retries for transient transport errors.
findings.failure_scenario: The coordinator presents a certificate whose fingerprint differs from the stored pin. The worker stays running and retries indefinitely without reporting the fingerprint mismatch.

verification.evidence: src/workers/tls.ts:114–115 rejects a mismatched pin with `new Error("Coordinator certificate fingerprint changed")`. src/workers/client.ts:146–148 catches every request exception and returns `undefined`; lines 157–158 then sleep and retry, with delay capped at 10 seconds.
verification.trigger: A coordinator certificate differs from the stored fingerprint while the worker remains running. Every mismatch is silently swallowed and retried indefinitely, hiding the reason the worker cannot connect.

findings.title: The credential test does not establish worker-side redaction
findings.detail: The worker and coordinator run in the same process and share the credential registry. The test registers the secret globally and checks only the stored coordinator result and events, so coordinator-side sanitization can make it pass even if the worker sends the credential in plaintext.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the outgoing worker event and result bodies before coordinator processing, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator.
findings.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction is removed and a gate prints a worker-only credential; the shared coordinator registry still redacts the stored output, so this test passes while the credential crosses the connection.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:659 registers `registerCredential("WORKER_OUTPUT_TEST", secret)` in the test process; :459 invokes `runWorker(...)` in that same process. Assertions at :681–683 inspect only stored `result` and `events`. src/db/workers.ts:59 calls `redactGateData(data)`, and :291 stores `JSON.stringify(this.sanitize(run))`. src/util/proc.ts:667 defines the shared module-level `credentialValues` registry.
verification.trigger: A regression allowing raw worker output onto the connection can remain undetected because the coordinator shares the credential registry and sanitizes stored output. The test never asserts that outgoing event/result payloads are already redacted.

findings.title: The bundle test never exercises distinct head and base commits
findings.detail: The shared request fixture assigns the same commit to headSha and baseSha. Consequently, the end-to-end bundle test cannot detect an implementation that bundles only the head, even though the request requires both commits to be available on the worker.
findings.suggestion: Create distinct base and head commits and have a worker gate verify that both requested commits are present.
findings.failure_scenario: Bundle creation omits baseSha when it differs from headSha; the existing end-to-end test still passes because its two SHAs are identical.

verification.evidence: test/workers.test.ts:123–124 sets both `baseSha: sha` and `headSha: sha`; the end-to-end test at :657 uses `request(true)`. src/server/workers.ts:88 currently includes both via `new Set([request.headSha, request.baseSha].filter(Boolean))`, but the fixture exercises only one distinct SHA.
verification.trigger: If bundle creation regresses to including only headSha, the existing end-to-end test still passes because baseSha equals headSha. It cannot establish that a distinct base commit is included.

findings.title: Reconcile streamed check failures with the final result
findings.detail: The coordinator validates each check event and the final GateRun independently. It accepts a passing final result even if the same lease previously reported that check as failed. The failed event is stored, but it does not influence the returned GateRun, so an inconsistent worker response can turn an observed failure into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Validate the final run against the check events recorded for the current lease and treat inconsistent results as an infrastructure failure.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid failed event for a requested check, then posts a valid GateRun reporting that same check as passed; the coordinator completes the job with the passing result.

verification.evidence: src/server/workers.ts:130 validates the final result using only `!validRun(request, result.data.run)`. Lines 135-136 independently store events or complete the job: `if (action === "events" && event.success) workers.event(id, event.data); else if (result.success) workers.complete(id, result.data.run);`. src/workers/validation.ts:44-49 checks requested check membership and setup consistency without consulting stored events. src/gates/lan.ts:72 returns the stored final result: `if (job.state === "done" && job.result) return JSON.parse(job.result) as GateRun;`.
verification.trigger: A lease-holding worker submits a valid failed check event, then a schema-valid passing result for the same requested check and SHA. No reconciliation occurs, so the job completes with the contradictory passing result.

findings.title: Coordinator-only credentials can be truncated before redaction
findings.detail: runLocalGates truncates output on the worker after redacting only credentials registered on that worker. The coordinator subsequently redacts the already-truncated value using its own credentials. If the tail boundary cuts through a coordinator credential that the worker does not know, the coordinator sees only a fragment and literal credential redaction cannot remove it before the event or result is stored.
findings.suggestion: Ensure coordinator-only credentials cannot be cut before coordinator-side redaction, such as by sending bounded raw output with enough overlap for coordinator redaction before applying the final output limit.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate prints a coordinator credential unknown to the worker, followed by enough output that the 6,000-character tail starts in the middle of that credential. The credential suffix is sent to and stored by the coordinator.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:114 redacts using the worker's registered credentials, then line 126 truncates with `combined.slice(-OUTPUT_TAIL)`; line 74 sets `OUTPUT_TAIL = 6_000`. src/workers/client.ts:233 sends that truncated run. src/db/workers.ts:58–60 sanitizes received data, and lines 288–291 persist it. src/util/proc.ts:683–684 redacts by matching complete registered secret strings: `text.split(secret).join("[redacted]")`.
verification.trigger: A gate prints a credential known only to the coordinator, with trailing output positioning the tail boundary inside the credential. The worker sends only its suffix; coordinator redaction cannot match the complete credential, so the suffix is persisted unredacted.

findings.title: A failed check from a lost lease can become a pass
findings.detail: The request says infrastructure retries must “never turn a failing check into a pass.” Check events from an attempt are streamed to hooks, but after that attempt loses its lease the final verdict uses only the later worker's GateRun. A failed check already reported by the first worker is therefore discarded for verdict purposes.
findings.suggestion: Retain completed check failures across infrastructure attempts and ensure a later passing result cannot erase them.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing check event, disconnects before posting its GateRun, and the replacement worker reports that check as passing. The returned GateRun marks it as passing.

verification.evidence: src/db/workers.ts:257–260 requeues a lost lease with `j.attempt < 2 ? verification.trigger: The first worker reports a failed check and loses its lease before completion. A second worker leases the same job and submits a valid passing GateRun. That passing GateRun becomes the returned result despite the earlier failed check.

findings.title: Restart discards leased retry and timeout jobs

A persisted timeout or retry job is cancelled and replaced when its stage resumes, even if the worker is still running or has completed it.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts:29–37 requires `pending.purpose === purpose` and `["baseline", "initial", "rebase"].includes(purpose)` to reuse a handle; otherwise it calls `cancelGateExecution(pending.handle, ctx.deps.gateExecutor)`. The retry has no deadline.
candidates.suggestion: Classify request errors and propagate certificate validation and configuration failures; bound retries for transient transport errors.
candidates.failure_scenario: The coordinator presents a certificate whose fingerprint differs from the stored pin. The worker stays running and retries indefinitely without reporting the fingerprint mismatch.

candidates.title: The credential test does not establish worker-side redaction
candidates.detail: The worker and coordinator run in the same process and share the credential registry. The test registers the secret globally and checks only the stored coordinator result and events, so coordinator-side sanitization can make it pass even if the worker sends the credential in plaintext.
candidates.suggestion: Inspect the outgoing worker event and result bodies before coordinator processing, or run the worker in a separate process with a credential unknown to the coordinator.
candidates.failure_scenario: Worker-side redaction is removed and a gate prints a worker-only credential; the shared coordinator registry still redacts the stored output, so this test passes while the credential crosses the connection.

candidates.title: The bundle test never exercises distinct head and base commits
candidates.detail: The shared request fixture assigns the same commit to headSha and baseSha. Consequently, the end-to-end bundle test cannot detect an implementation that bundles only the head, even though the request requires both commits to be available on the worker.
candidates.suggestion: Create distinct base and head commits and have a worker gate verify that both requested commits are present.
candidates.failure_scenario: Bundle creation omits baseSha when it differs from headSha; the existing end-to-end test still passes because its two SHAs are identical.

candidates.title: Reconcile streamed check failures with the final result
candidates.detail: The coordinator validates each check event and the final GateRun independently. It accepts a passing final result even if the same lease previously reported that check as failed. The failed event is stored, but it does not influence the returned GateRun, so an inconsistent worker response can turn an observed failure into a pass.
candidates.suggestion: Validate the final run against the check events recorded for the current lease and treat inconsistent results as an infrastructure failure.
candidates.failure_scenario: A worker posts a valid failed event for a requested check, then posts a valid GateRun reporting that same check as passed; the coordinator completes the job with the passing result.

candidates.title: Coordinator-only credentials can be truncated before redaction
candidates.detail: runLocalGates truncates output on the worker after redacting only credentials registered on that worker. The coordinator subsequently redacts the already-truncated value using its own credentials. If the tail boundary cuts through a coordinator credential that the worker does not know, the coordinator sees only a fragment and literal credential redaction cannot remove it before the event or result is stored.
candidates.suggestion: Ensure coordinator-only credentials cannot be cut before coordinator-side redaction, such as by sending bounded raw output with enough overlap for coordinator redaction before applying the final output limit.
candidates.failure_scenario: A gate prints a coordinator credential unknown to the worker, followed by enough output that the 6,000-character tail starts in the middle of that credential. The credential suffix is sent to and stored by the coordinator.

candidates.title: A failed check from a lost lease can become a pass
candidates.detail: The request says infrastructure retries must “never turn a failing check into a pass.” Check events from an attempt are streamed to hooks, but after that attempt loses its lease the final verdict uses only the later worker's GateRun. candidates.suggestion: Retain completed check failures across infrastructure attempts and ensure a later passing result cannot erase them.
candidates.failure_scenario: A worker posts a failing check event, disconnects before posting its GateRun, and the replacement worker reports that check as passing. The returned GateRun marks it as passing.

candidates.title: Restart discards leased retry and timeout jobs
candidates.detail: The request says `attach` waits for the stored result so “a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.” Resume is restricted to baseline, initial and rebase purposes. candidates.suggestion: Provide durable resume handling for every LAN gate execution purpose, preserving the original job identity and any state needed to consume its result.

findings.title: A dirty worktree can bypass detection of a cancelled worker's push
findings.detail: When reconciliation rejects an open job, the executor cancels it and calls prepare(). If the coordinator worktree is dirty, prepare() returns null before checking the remote branch, so the executor runs the local session even if the cancelled worker already pushed an unreported commit. The request requires that case to end NeedsHuman.
findings.suggestion: Check the cancelled job's remote branch for an unreported push before falling back to local execution, including when preparation cannot proceed because the worktree is dirty.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes W but has not reported it; after restart the coordinator worktree is dirty. Reconciliation cancels the leased job, prepare() returns null, and a local session starts instead of reporting the unaccepted push.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1138-1139 requires HEAD to match and `(await clean())` for resume. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:89-91 then executes `workers.cancelAgentJob(id)` and `id = undefined` when reconciliation fails. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1149 returns early with `if (!(await clean())) return null;`, before checking the remote at line 1150. src/pipeline/lan-agent.ts:110 executes `if (!prepared) return fallback();`; line 51 defines fallback as calling `local()` when not aborted. The unaccepted-push check at lines 203-208 is therefore bypassed.
verification.trigger: A stored leased worker job has pushed W without an accepted report, and the coordinator worktree is dirty on restart. Resume fails cleanliness, cancels the job and discards its id; prepare returns null before inspecting the remote, so a local session starts instead of raising NeedsHuman for the unaccepted push.

findings.title: A fenced pending report no longer renews its lease
findings.detail: The new result request survives the fence, but the fence aborts the job controller and heldJobs() consequently omits the job from heartbeats. Those heartbeats no longer renew its lease. If result requests remain unavailable while heartbeat requests succeed, the lease expires despite the worker continuing to retry the accepted-report request, and the coordinator rejects the eventual report.
findings.suggestion: Keep a pushed job in the heartbeat's held-job list while its independently bounded result report is pending, until the result is accepted or the lease is explicitly lost.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes during an outage and its fence fires. After restart, heartbeats succeed but result requests fail transiently for longer than the remaining lease or restart grace. The coordinator expires the job; a later result receives 409 and the pushed commit cannot be adopted.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:565-566: the fence executes `job.controller.abort()`. At :501-504, `heldJobs()` filters on `job.reported && !job.controller.signal.aborted`; heartbeats send `jobs: heldJobs()` (:546). src/db/workers.ts:242-252 renews leases only `for (const id of c.jobs)`. At :415-420, an expired lease triggers `this.failAgentJob(j.id, "Lease expired")`. src/server/workers.ts:202-203 rejects results without a held lease with 409.
verification.trigger: A pushed result continues retrying after the fence fires. Successful heartbeats omit its aborted job, so its lease is never renewed. If result failures outlast the lease/restart grace, the coordinator expires the job and rejects the eventual report, leaving the pushed commit without an accepted report.

findings.title: Late result retries can prevent worker shutdown
findings.detail: The late-result signal excludes the worker's shutdown signal as well as the job cancellation and fence signals. If the coordinator is unreachable, `call()` keeps retrying until the attempt deadline, while `runWorker` waits for every job task in its shutdown cleanup. Stopping the worker can therefore hang for the remainder of the agent attempt, potentially many minutes.
findings.suggestion: Combine the attempt-deadline signal with the worker's shutdown signal while continuing to exclude the job controller used by cancellation and the fence.
findings.failure_scenario: A worker pushes a commit, begins retrying its result during a coordinator outage, and then receives a shutdown signal. Its result request remains active and `runWorker` does not finish until the attempt deadline expires.

verification.evidence: src/workers/client.ts:861 uses `AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now()))` alone for a pushed result. The retry loop uses only `requestSignal` (:508-525). Shutdown aborts job controllers (:984-986), then awaits `...allJobs().map(([, j]) => j.task)` (:987-990). src/cli/main.ts:383-384 handles SIGINT/SIGTERM by aborting the worker controller.
verification.trigger: After a push, result requests keep failing during an outage and the worker receives SIGINT/SIGTERM. The result retry ignores both shutdown and job-controller cancellation, so runWorker waits until the attempt deadline unless the request succeeds or receives a definitive refusal first.

findings.title: Queued restart test completes the job before the scheduler resumes
findings.detail: The queued case leases and reports the job before calling resumed.start(), so the resumed executor sees a done job. It does not exercise reattachment to a queued job followed by pickup and completion after restart.
findings.suggestion: Start the resumed factory while the job is still queued, observe reattachment, then lease and complete that same ID and assert that no second row is created.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that replaces a stored queued job on resume could pass this integration case because the stored job has already become done.

Existing adoptWorkerCommit tests exercise the ordinary adoption path.

findings.detail: The request says “a worker that stays unreachable for one lease period after the restart is retried on another worker.” Although the lease-expiry calculation grants 60 seconds, this freshness check fails the job after 30 seconds without a heartbeat. That can discard a worker’s pushed result before the promised lease period has elapsed. The requested freshness formula also specifies this 30-second behavior, so the requirements conflict and need to be reconciled.

Verifier: 21 candidates, 21 checked, 4 refuted.

findings.title: Lifecycle transitions can disappear between polls
findings.detail: Comments are derived from the current run status, and an event is persisted only when reconciliation observes that status. A run that enters needs_human and is resumed or resolved before the next poll never records or posts that event. Likewise, a second needs_human episode is suppressed by the first episode's done checkpoint. This does not provide a durable side effect for each transition across restarts or polling intervals.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle events durably when transitions occur, with an identity for each status episode, and reconcile those records independently of the current status.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters needs_human and the owner resumes it before the next queue poll; no needs-you comment is posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:101–102: `if (run.status === "needs_human") events.set("needs_human", ...)`; line 113: `if (!events.has(event) && state(effect) !== "pending") continue;`. src/db/store.ts:2037–2038 allows `needs_human` to become `resolved`.
verification.trigger: A run enters needs_human and is resolved before reconciliation observes it. No pending comment was recorded, so the required needs-you comment and reason disappear. Here, owner resolution is the supported interpretation of ending the needs_human state.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates only run for queue-enabled repositories
findings.detail: Both the reconciler and its timer are conditional on the issue queue's repository and trusted-account configuration. Runs started through CLI, MCP, or GitHub triggers in any other configured repository therefore receive no lifecycle labels or comments, even though the requested behavior covers every start path and does not require queue admission to be enabled.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and select linked issues according to the supported repository settings.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository has the GitHub integration configured but is absent from githubQueue.repos; a CLI run with `Closes #42` produces no lifecycle updates.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:10–12: `lifecycleManaged` requires `cfg.githubQueue?.trusted.length` and membership in `cfg.githubQueue.repos`; line 43: `if (!lifecycleManaged(cfg, repo)) continue;`. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:144 also returns immediately when queue configuration is absent.
verification.trigger: A CLI run contains Closes #42 for a GitHub-integrated repository absent from githubQueue.repos. Reconciliation skips it, producing none of the required lifecycle labels or comments.

findings.title: A partial failure can release an issue before its failure label is applied

A failed CLI or MCP run linked through `Closes #n` has no such reference. Until the failed label is successfully written, the queue therefore sees neither the failure label nor that latest failed run and can select the issue without re-approval.
candidates.suggestion: Include all linked-issue runs in the existing eligibility/admission evidence, including runs linked through their prompt.
candidates.failure_scenario: A CLI run for `Closes #7` fails, the GitHub failed-label write errors, and the issue still has its previously approved priority label; the same poll can create a queue run for it.

candidates.title: Re-approval in the same timestamp second is rejected
candidates.detail: The requirement specifies the labeled events' order and actor. Comparing parsed timestamps with strict greater-than rejects a trusted priority event that follows the failure event but has the same timestamp precision, even though the timeline preserves their order.
candidates.suggestion: Use the ordered timeline events to determine whether a trusted priority application follows the failure event, including ties in timestamps.
candidates.failure_scenario: GitHub records the failure label and a subsequent trusted priority label with the same second in `createdAt`; the issue remains ineligible.

Verifier: 19 candidates, 19 checked, 5 refuted.

findings.title: Status transitions between polls are lost
findings.detail: Comments and labels are derived only from the run's current status. No durable event is recorded when a run enters needs_human or failed, so a transition that ends before the next poll cannot be reconstructed. The single comment key for each status also suppresses later occurrences of the same status.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle transitions durably when they occur and reconcile each recorded occurrence independently.
findings.failure_scenario: A run enters needs_human and is resumed before the next queue poll. The poll sees running and never posts the needs-you comment or applies its label. A second needs_human episode after an observed first episode also receives no new comment.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:101–102 only creates the event when `run.status === "needs_human"`. Lines 112–114 use `const effect = `comment:${event}`` and `if (state(effect) === "done") continue;`, permanently deduplicating that event across all episodes of a run.
verification.trigger: A needs_human episode starts and ends between polls, so its label and comment are never recorded. After one observed episode completes its comment, subsequent needs_human episodes never receive another comment.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-configured repositories
findings.detail: The reconciler skips every repository that is absent from githubQueue.repos or has no trusted queue accounts, and it is not started at all when the queue is disabled. The requested lifecycle applies to runs started through every entry point; it is not limited to repositories enabled for automatic issue picking.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration for linked issues.
findings.failure_scenario: A user starts `limitless run` with `Closes #7` in a repository that has no issue queue configured. The run receives no lifecycle labels or comments.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:10–12 requires `!!cfg.githubQueue?.trusted.length` and membership in `cfg.githubQueue.repos`; line 43 skips other repositories with `if (!lifecycleManaged(cfg, repo)) continue;`. src/integrations/index.ts:66–67 starts the lifecycle-owning queue only when queue repositories and trusted accounts are configured.
verification.trigger: A CLI run containing Closes #7 targets a repository without issue queue configuration. Its lifecycle labels and comments are skipped despite the requirement covering every start path.

findings.title: A failed label write can allow a failed manual run to be re-picked
findings.detail: The transition removes in-progress before adding failed, and a write failure is caught before the queue continues to query candidates. The queue's latestIssueRun lookup only recognizes issue source references, so a terminal CLI or MCP run linked through `Closes #n` supplies no local re-approval guard.
findings.suggestion: Make admission account for terminal runs linked through all supported start paths, including while lifecycle writes are pending.
findings.failure_scenario: A CLI run for `Closes #7` fails. Removing in-progress succeeds, adding failed fails, and the issue still has its old trusted priority label. The same poll can pick it again without a new approval.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:13 orders labels as in-progress, needs-you, failed; lines 68–86 remove in-progress before adding failed, and lines 93–95 only log write failures. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:191 reconciles before selecting candidates. src/db/store.ts:1268–1270 limits `latestIssueRun` to `json_extract(runs.source_ref, '$.kind') = 'issue'`, excluding ordinary CLI prompt links.
verification.trigger: A failed CLI run linked through Closes #7 has no issue sourceRef. Removing in-progress succeeds but adding failed fails. With its original trusted priority approval still present, neither a status label nor latestIssueRun prevents the queue from immediately picking the issue again.

findings.title: An older run can overwrite labels after a newer run starts
findings.detail: The latest-run map is computed once before any GitHub awaits. Re-reading the old run's status does not check whether another run has since claimed the same issue, so an in-flight reconciliation can apply an old terminal label after a newer run has started.
findings.suggestion: Recheck issue ownership after awaited operations and before each label mutation, coordinating it with run admission.
findings.failure_scenario: While reconciliation of an old failed run is awaiting its label read, a new run for the same issue starts. The old reconciliation then removes in-progress or adds failed based on its stale latest-run map.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:35–39 builds `latest` once from `store.issueLifecycleRuns()`. Line 56 checks that snapshot before the awaited label read at line 60. Lines 63–71 re-read only the old run and check `desiredLabel(run) !== target`; they never recheck whether another run now owns the issue.
verification.trigger: A newer run for the same issue starts while an old terminal run awaits GitHub's label response. The old reconciliation can then remove in-progress or add failed using its stale ownership snapshot, displaying the old run's state until a later reconciliation.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-enabled repositories
findings.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation skips every repository absent from githubQueue.repos, and the reconciler itself is started only when the queue has configured repositories and trusted accounts. The request requires lifecycle updates for every start path, including CLI and MCP runs, with gh as the fallback identity.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and handle linked issues for all applicable repositories.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs `limitless run` with `Closes #7` for a repository that is not in githubQueue.repos. No lifecycle label or comment is posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:12 requires `cfg.githubQueue.repos.some((r) => r.toLowerCase() === repo.toLowerCase())`; line 43 executes `if (!lifecycleManaged(cfg, repo)) continue;` before any lifecycle writes.
verification.trigger: A CLI run containing Closes #7 targets a repository absent from githubQueue.repos. No lifecycle labels or comments are posted for that run.

findings.title: Transient lifecycle events disappear before they are checkpointed
findings.detail: Events are inferred only from the current run snapshot. A needs_human or failed state that begins and ends between polls is never recorded. The same loss occurs when an earlier comment fails: the loop breaks before saving later events as pending, so a status change before the next poll erases them.
findings.suggestion: Durably record each lifecycle transition when it occurs, then reconcile its effects independently of the current status.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human while the started comment write is failing, then is resumed before the next poll. No needs-you comment is ever posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:101–102 adds needs_human only when `run.status === "needs_human"`; :165–167 handles an earlier comment failure with `failure(error); break;`, before later events are checkpointed. src/db/store.ts:2037–2040 allows needs_human to become resolved.
verification.trigger: The started comment fails while the run needs human input, so the needs_human event is never checkpointed. If the owner resolves the run before the next poll, its required reason comment is permanently lost.

findings.title: An unrelated comment can impersonate a completed lifecycle write
findings.detail: Recovery treats any issue comment containing the predictable marker as proof that the factory posted its pending comment, without checking its author. An issue participant can supply that marker and cause the actual lifecycle comment to be permanently marked done.
findings.suggestion: Verify the recovered comment was authored by the configured factory identity and matches the pending body before marking the effect done.
findings.failure_scenario: After a comment POST fails, another issue participant posts a comment containing the run's marker. On the next poll the factory records the failed comment as delivered and never retries it.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:123 parses comments as `z.object({ body: z.string() })`; :128–130 uses only `comments.some((c) => c.body.includes(marker))` to `save(effect, "done")` and skip posting.
verification.trigger: A comment POST fails before acceptance. Another participant posts the predictable marker. The retry accepts that unrelated comment as completion without checking its author or intended body, permanently suppressing the factory comment.

findings.title: A 404 during label removal is silently recorded as success
findings.detail: The catch treats every HTTP 404 as an already-removed label. GitHub can also return 404 for an inaccessible repository or issue, so a permission or installation failure can be checkpointed as a successful label transition and will not be retried.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the label is absent with a successful fresh read before recording the removal as complete; otherwise log and retry the error.
findings.failure_scenario: The initial label read succeeds, but the App loses repository access before the DELETE. GitHub returns 404 and the reconciliation cursor records the label set as complete even though the label remains.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:85–88 suppresses DELETE errors matching `HTTP 404` and then executes `save(effect, "done")`. :92 saves the complete label cursor; :56 skips reconciliation when that cursor equals the desired label.
verification.trigger: After a successful label read, access is lost and label removal returns HTTP 404. For a transition requiring only removals, such as cancellation, the unchanged labels are recorded as reconciled, without logging or retrying the failed removal.

findings.title: Status transitions between polls never produce their comments
findings.detail: Lifecycle comments are derived from the current run status. A needs_human episode that begins and ends between polls is never recorded as pending, so its required comment is permanently lost. The pending-comment tests cover a transition only after a poll has already observed it.
findings.suggestion: Record lifecycle events durably when transitions occur and reconcile those records. Add a test that enters and leaves needs_human between polls, then restarts and checks for exactly one comment.
findings.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human and is resumed before the next issue-queue poll; no needs-you comment is posted.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:97–102 reads current state and constructs needs_human events only from `run.status === "needs_human"`; :113 skips absent events unless already pending. src/db/store.ts:2037–2040 permits needs_human → resolved. Reconciliation runs from the poll at src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:191.
verification.trigger: A run enters needs_human and is resolved before the next poll. No comment checkpoint exists, and the reconciler never examines the earlier transition, so the required needs-you comment is omitted. Retrying creates a new run rather than resuming this one, but resolution demonstrates the claimed missed-transition defect.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside the issue queue configuration
findings.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation requires the repository to be in githubQueue.repos with trusted accounts configured, and the poller does not start without that configuration. The request requires updates for linked runs from all start paths. The new test explicitly asserts no updates for disabled or unlisted repositories, thereby protecting this omission.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation for linked GitHub issues independently of queue admission configuration, and test a CLI or MCP run when queue polling is disabled.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner starts a run with Closes #7 in a GitHub repository that is not enabled for automatic issue picking; the issue receives neither labels nor comments.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:10-12: `lifecycleManaged` requires `!!cfg.githubQueue?.trusted.length` and membership in `cfg.githubQueue.repos`; line 43: `if (!lifecycleManaged(cfg, repo)) continue;`. src/integrations/issue-queue.ts:144 also returns immediately when queue configuration is absent.
verification.trigger: Start a CLI run containing Closes #7 in a repository outside githubQueue.repos. Reconciliation skips the issue, so it receives no lifecycle labels or comments despite the requirement covering every start path.

findings.title: Restart coverage does not exercise each lifecycle transition
findings.detail: The interruption matrix only interrupts the initial started event. The needs-human, failure, cancellation, PR, and merge tests restart after their writes have completed, so they do not establish that a restart between each transition's label change and comment preserves the required effect.
findings.suggestion: Exercise interruption after the label update and before the comment for each applicable transition, then reopen the store and verify the final labels and exactly one comment.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that loses a failed or needs-human comment after its label write can pass the current restart tests.

verification.evidence: test/issue-queue.test.ts:1275 parameterizes interruption only by ["after label", "after comment"]; its assertions at :1295–1298 cover only "limitless:in-progress" and "comment:started". The terminal-status tests assert both comments exist before restarting (:1225–1229). Additional failed/needs_human restart tests begin with the comment already checkpointed: :1347 asserts `issueLifecycleEffect(..., `comment:${status}`)).toBe("pending")` before :1349 calls `h.stop()`. None interrupts those transitions between the label write and comment checkpoint.
verification.trigger: A regression affecting failed or needs_human comment recovery specifically after its label write but before its comment checkpoint could pass the current restart tests; that interruption window is exercised only for run start.

findings.title: Do not accept an arbitrary issue comment as proof of a factory write
findings.detail: Recovery treats any comment containing the predictable lifecycle marker as proof that the factory posted its comment. Issue comments are untrusted: their author is neither retrieved nor checked. An attacker who can comment can therefore suppress a pending lifecycle notification.
findings.suggestion: Authenticate the author of a matching comment against the GitHub identity used for the write, and require an exact, validated marker before recording the effect as done.
findings.failure_scenario: A comment POST fails or the daemon restarts after marking it pending. Another issue participant posts a comment containing `<!-- limitless-lifecycle:<run-id>:failed -->`. On the next poll, reconciliation marks the failed notification done without posting it.

verification.evidence: src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:120-129 constructs `<!-- limitless-lifecycle:${run.id}:${event} -->`, parses comments as `z.object({ body: z.string() })`, then uses `comments.some((c) => c.body.includes(marker))` to `save(effect, "done")`. No author or identity is checked.
verification.trigger: A failed POST leaves a notification pending. Another participant posts its predictable marker. The next poll treats that participant's comment as the factory notification and permanently suppresses the intended comment.

findings.title: Lifecycle updates are limited to repositories in the issue queue
findings.detail: The request covers “any start path,” but reconciliation skips every repository outside `githubQueue.repos`, and the reconciler is not started at all when the queue is disabled. A CLI, MCP, label-triggered, or comment-triggered run against another repository therefore receives none of the required lifecycle labels or comments.
findings.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and cover linked issues from every supported start path.
findings.failure_scenario: A user starts `limitless run` with `Closes #12` for a repository that is not configured in `githubQueue.repos`; no in-progress label or lifecycle comments are posted.

verification.trigger: Start limitless run with Closes #12 for a repository absent from githubQueue.repos. No in-progress label or lifecycle comments are written. This is the same underlying defect as C13.

findings.title: Transitions occurring between polls are never recorded
findings.detail: The requirement says each lifecycle event is a durable side effect and must not lose a label change or comment across restarts. The reconciler derives needs-human, failed, and cancelled events solely from the current run status; it creates no pending effect when the transition occurs. If the run advances again before the next poll, that event is permanently invisible.
findings.suggestion: Durably enqueue lifecycle effects at the state transition and reconcile those recorded effects on each poll.

Lines 2037-2040 allow needs_human runs to transition to `resolved`.

No pending lifecycle effect exists, so subsequent polls permanently omit its needs-you label and reason comment. The reconciler does not replay persisted status history.
