candidates.failure_scenario: A run enters needs_human and is resumed before the next queue poll. The poll sees running and never posts the needs-you comment or applies its label. A second needs_human episode after an observed first episode also receives no new comment.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-configured repositories
candidates.detail: The reconciler skips every repository that is absent from githubQueue.repos or has no trusted queue accounts, and it is not started at all when the queue is disabled. The requested lifecycle applies to runs started through every entry point; it is not limited to repositories enabled for automatic issue picking.
candidates.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration for linked issues.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user starts `limitless run` with `Closes #7` in a repository that has no issue queue configured. The run receives no lifecycle labels or comments.

candidates.title: A failed label write can allow a failed manual run to be re-picked
candidates.detail: The transition removes in-progress before adding failed, and a write failure is caught before the queue continues to query candidates. The queue's latestIssueRun lookup only recognizes issue source references, so a terminal CLI or MCP run linked through `Closes #n` supplies no local re-approval guard.
candidates.suggestion: Make admission account for terminal runs linked through all supported start paths, including while lifecycle writes are pending.
candidates.failure_scenario: A CLI run for `Closes #7` fails. Removing in-progress succeeds, adding failed fails, and the issue still has its old trusted priority label. The same poll can pick it again without a new approval.

candidates.title: An older run can overwrite labels after a newer run starts
candidates.detail: The latest-run map is computed once before any GitHub awaits. Re-reading the old run's status does not check whether another run has since claimed the same issue, so an in-flight reconciliation can apply an old terminal label after a newer run has started.
candidates.suggestion: Recheck issue ownership after awaited operations and before each label mutation, coordinating it with run admission.
candidates.failure_scenario: While reconciliation of an old failed run is awaiting its label read, a new run for the same issue starts. The old reconciliation then removes in-progress or adds failed based on its stale latest-run map.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside queue-enabled repositories
candidates.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation skips every repository absent from githubQueue.repos, and the reconciler itself is started only when the queue has configured repositories and trusted accounts. The request requires lifecycle updates for every start path, including CLI and MCP runs, with gh as the fallback identity.
candidates.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and handle linked issues for all applicable repositories.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user runs `limitless run` with `Closes #7` for a repository that is not in githubQueue.repos. No lifecycle label or comment is posted.

candidates.title: Transient lifecycle events disappear before they are checkpointed
candidates.detail: Events are inferred only from the current run snapshot. A needs_human or failed state that begins and ends between polls is never recorded. The same loss occurs when an earlier comment fails: the loop breaks before saving later events as pending, so a status change before the next poll erases them.
candidates.suggestion: Durably record each lifecycle transition when it occurs, then reconcile its effects independently of the current status.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human while the started comment write is failing, then is resumed before the next poll. No needs-you comment is ever posted.

candidates.title: A second needs-human episode is treated as already delivered
candidates.detail: Comment checkpoints are keyed only by run and event name. Once a needs_human comment is marked done, a resumed run that later reaches needs_human again cannot post its new reason. Label reconciliation can still switch back to needs-you, leaving the issue with a stale explanation.
candidates.suggestion: Key lifecycle effects by a durable transition or status episode rather than only by event type.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run needs human input, resumes after the owner responds, and later needs human input for a different reason. The second reason is never commented.

candidates.title: Re-approval can come from a priority label that is no longer applied
candidates.detail: The post-failure check accepts any trusted priority labeled event, even if that label was subsequently removed. The separate approved check can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before the failure, so the current approval need not be the one applied after failure.
candidates.suggestion: Require a currently applied, trusted priority label whose latest application occurred after the failure label.
candidates.failure_scenario: Priority:2 was applied before failure; a trusted user applies and removes priority:1 after failure. The issue remains eligible using the old priority:2 label despite the later approval having been withdrawn.

candidates.title: An unrelated comment can impersonate a completed lifecycle write
candidates.detail: Recovery treats any issue comment containing the predictable marker as proof that the factory posted its pending comment, without checking its author. An issue participant can supply that marker and cause the actual lifecycle comment to be permanently marked done.
candidates.suggestion: Verify the recovered comment was authored by the configured factory identity and matches the pending body before marking the effect done.
candidates.failure_scenario: After a comment POST fails, another issue participant posts a comment containing the run's marker. On the next poll the factory records the failed comment as delivered and never retries it.

candidates.title: A 404 during label removal is silently recorded as success
candidates.detail: The catch treats every HTTP 404 as an already-removed label. GitHub can also return 404 for an inaccessible repository or issue, so a permission or installation failure can be checkpointed as a successful label transition and will not be retried.
candidates.suggestion: Confirm the label is absent with a successful fresh read before recording the removal as complete; otherwise log and retry the error.
candidates.failure_scenario: The initial label read succeeds, but the App loses repository access before the DELETE. GitHub returns 404 and the reconciliation cursor records the label set as complete even though the label remains.

candidates.title: Status transitions between polls never produce their comments
candidates.detail: Lifecycle comments are derived from the current run status. A needs_human episode that begins and ends between polls is never recorded as pending, so its required comment is permanently lost. The pending-comment tests cover a transition only after a poll has already observed it.
candidates.suggestion: Record lifecycle events durably when transitions occur and reconcile those records. Add a test that enters and leaves needs_human between polls, then restarts and checks for exactly one comment.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run reaches needs_human and is resumed before the next issue-queue poll; no needs-you comment is posted.

candidates.title: A removed priority label can supply re-approval
candidates.detail: The re-approval check accepts any trusted priority-label event after failure, even if that label is no longer present. The separate approved-label check can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before failure. The tests only exercise re-approval using the currently present label and miss this combination.
candidates.suggestion: Require a currently applied, trusted priority label whose applicable labeling event is later than the failure event. Add a test with an old current priority and a later trusted priority that has since been removed.
candidates.failure_scenario: priority:1 remains from before failure; a trusted user adds and then removes priority:2 after failure. The issue becomes eligible despite having no current priority approval applied after failure.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are disabled outside the issue queue configuration
candidates.detail: Lifecycle reconciliation requires the repository to be in githubQueue.repos with trusted accounts configured, and the poller does not start without that configuration. The request requires updates for linked runs from all start paths. The new test explicitly asserts no updates for disabled or unlisted repositories, thereby protecting this omission.
candidates.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation for linked GitHub issues independently of queue admission configuration, and test a CLI or MCP run when queue polling is disabled.
candidates.failure_scenario: An owner starts a run with Closes #7 in a GitHub repository that is not enabled for automatic issue picking; the issue receives neither labels nor comments.

candidates.title: Restart coverage does not exercise each lifecycle transition
candidates.detail: The interruption matrix only interrupts the initial started event. The needs-human, failure, cancellation, PR, and merge tests restart after their writes have completed, so they do not establish that a restart between each transition's label change and comment preserves the required effect.
candidates.suggestion: Exercise interruption after the label update and before the comment for each applicable transition, then reopen the store and verify the final labels and exactly one comment.
candidates.failure_scenario: A regression that loses a failed or needs-human comment after its label write can pass the current restart tests.

candidates.title: Do not accept an arbitrary issue comment as proof of a factory write
candidates.detail: Recovery treats any comment containing the predictable lifecycle marker as proof that the factory posted its comment. Issue comments are untrusted: their author is neither retrieved nor checked. An attacker who can comment can therefore suppress a pending lifecycle notification.
candidates.suggestion: Authenticate the author of a matching comment against the GitHub identity used for the write, and require an exact, validated marker before recording the effect as done.
candidates.failure_scenario: A comment POST fails or the daemon restarts after marking it pending. Another issue participant posts a comment containing `<!-- limitless-lifecycle:<run-id>:failed -->`. On the next poll, reconciliation marks the failed notification done without posting it.

candidates.title: Tie re-approval to a priority label that is still applied
candidates.detail: The post-failure check accepts any historical trusted priority-label event, even if that label has since been removed. The separately computed `approved` set can be satisfied by a different priority label applied before the failure, so a withdrawn re-approval still permits the issue to run.
candidates.suggestion: Require the latest trusted application of a currently applied priority label to be later than the failure event.
candidates.failure_scenario: An issue retains `priority:2` from before failure. A trusted account applies `priority:1` after failure and subsequently removes it to withdraw approval. The old `priority:2` satisfies `approved`, while the historical `priority:1` event satisfies this check, so the failed issue is picked again.

candidates.title: Lifecycle updates are limited to repositories in the issue queue
candidates.detail: The request covers “any start path,” but reconciliation skips every repository outside `githubQueue.repos`, and the reconciler is not started at all when the queue is disabled. A CLI, MCP, label-triggered, or comment-triggered run against another repository therefore receives none of the required lifecycle labels or comments.
candidates.suggestion: Run lifecycle reconciliation independently of queue admission configuration and cover linked issues from every supported start path.
candidates.failure_scenario: A user starts `limitless run` with `Closes #12` for a repository that is not configured in `githubQueue.repos`; no in-progress label or lifecycle comments are posted.

candidates.title: Transitions occurring between polls are never recorded
candidates.detail: The requirement says each lifecycle event is a durable side effect and must not lose a label change or comment across restarts. The reconciler derives needs-human, failed, and cancelled events solely from the current run status; it creates no pending effect when the transition occurs. If the run advances again before the next poll, that event is permanently invisible.
candidates.suggestion: Durably enqueue lifecycle effects at the state transition and reconcile those recorded effects on each poll.
candidates.failure_scenario: A run reaches `needs_human` and is resumed before the next queue poll, or the daemon restarts and the run is resumed before reconciliation. No needs-you label or reason comment is ever posted.

candidates.title: A removed priority label can satisfy re-approval
candidates.detail: The request requires a trusted priority application after the failure label. This check accepts any historical trusted priority event after failure, even if that priority label was subsequently removed. A different priority label that was already present before the failure can then supply `approved`, so the issue is picked without a currently applied post-failure approval.
candidates.suggestion: Require the post-failure trusted event to be the latest application of a currently present, approved priority label.
candidates.failure_scenario: An issue has trusted `priority:2` before failure; afterward a trusted account briefly applies and removes `priority:3`. The remaining pre-failure `priority:2` makes the issue eligible.

findings.title: Classify the moved tip before discarding a release intent
findings.detail: Every `moved` result from a replay marks the confirmed lease lost and clears the intent without examining the returned tip. The claim client can return `moved` for a malformed record or a valid record that does not meet the supersession conditions. Clearing the journal also makes the row forgettable, losing confirmed ownership history and the final release record.

findings.title: A superseded unsent question set can never be published later
findings.detail: An unsent question effect is permanently marked done when its run temporarily stops waiting. If the run later returns to waiting with the same unanswered question IDs, observe() sees the existing effect and never creates another publication. The same problem occurs after recovery establishes that a stale POST was not accepted. The run can therefore remain waiting indefinitely without its questions appearing on the issue.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish a superseded effect with no confirmed publication from a completed publication, and allow a fresh eligible waiting episode to publish the set after any uncertain prior POST has been recovered.

findings.title: Retired unsent question sets cannot be published if they become eligible again
findings.detail: Superseding an unsent question effect marks it done, and observe() will never create that effect again because it already exists. A temporary linkage or status change can therefore permanently suppress a question set that was never posted.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish superseded unsent effects from completed publications and allow the same set to be scheduled again when it becomes eligible.

findings.title: Privacy reinspection can close an uncertain POST without recovery
findings.detail: The pending body is reinspected before marker recovery, and any inspection failure immediately marks the effect done.
